nodes.label: Lapidary Working Rules
nodes.rationale: The canonical rule set. Encodes decisions expensive to reverse so agents read them before writing code in an area.

nodes.label: We Never Edit Geometry
nodes.rationale: Editing belongs to Rhino, Fusion, FreeCAD, Blender, Orca. Lapidary visualizes, measures, routes and versions; competing with a CAD kernel's editor is unwinnable for a solo project.

nodes.label: Never Delete User Data Implicitly
nodes.rationale: Delete is soft, purge is separate and explicit, blobs quarantine 30 days. Derivative cache eviction must never read as data loss, because a user who fears for their models has lost trust in the product.

nodes.label: Automatic Format Negotiation
nodes.rationale: Slicers get 3MF/STL, CAD gets STEP, the viewer gets glTF. Never hand a mesh to someone who needed B-rep.

nodes.label: Measurement Must Not Lie
nodes.rationale: Analytic values come from B-rep entities where available; mesh-derived numbers are labelled approximate in the UI, always, so a tessellated figure is never mistaken for a nominal one.

nodes.label: Versioning Is Perforce-Shaped, Not Git-Shaped
nodes.rationale: Three-way merge is undefined for a B-rep solid and textual diff is meaningless, so: immutable content-addressed snapshots, a lineage DAG, pessimistic locks, and geometric diff in place of textual diff.

nodes.label: Governance Is Opt-In Per Library
nodes.rationale: Hobby libraries have no revisions, states or approvals; flipping a library to controlled turns that machinery on. One architecture serves hobbyist STLs and industrial STEP assemblies.

nodes.label: The Application Is Free And Complete
nodes.rationale: No gated features in the app. Revenue comes from the server, fleet, support and cloud, which is why lapidary-api may never depend on lapidary-enterprise.
nodes.norm_label: the application is free and complete

nodes.label: Downloads Are Never Silently Converted
nodes.rationale: variant=original returns byte-identical ingested bytes; anything we produced is named *.lapidary.*, so a user always knows whether they hold their own file or ours.

nodes.label: Container-First Distribution
nodes.rationale: Podman and Docker. The Tauri app is a later phase and bundles only our own binaries, never Postgres and never OCCT, which removes the highest-risk bundling item from the plan.

nodes.label: No SQL Outside lapidary-db
nodes.rationale: Everything goes through repository traits, enforced by deny.toml wrappers rather than review, so SQL cannot leak into feature crates.

nodes.label: The Open Path Never Touches A Source File Or The Kernel
nodes.rationale: Opening a part reads metadata plus derivatives only. Parsing STEP on open is the failure mode this rule exists to forbid; it is what keeps first paint under 120 ms.
nodes.norm_label: the open path never touches a source file or the kernel

nodes.label: Hash First, Always
nodes.rationale: BLAKE3 before anything else in ingest; a known hash short-circuits the whole pipeline, which is what makes re-import feel free.

nodes.label: Generated Columns Are Explicitly STORED
nodes.rationale: PG 18 defaults generated columns to virtual, and virtual columns cannot be indexed, so the tsvector search column would silently lose its GIN index.

nodes.label: Content Addressing Is Not Authorization
nodes.rationale: Hashes leak into manifests, logs, bundles and support tickets. Knowing a blob hash must never be a capability; always check tenant plus part reachability.

nodes.label: Pin Everything
nodes.rationale: Exact image digests, Cargo.lock committed, GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs because tags are mutable and that mutability is actively exploited.

nodes.label: lapidary-api Is A Library That Builds A Router
nodes.rationale: One codebase, three artifacts, all thin shells over the same axum Router. Never a binary, never forked per distribution.
nodes.norm_label: lapidary-api is a library that builds a router

nodes.label: Prefer The Boring Option
nodes.rationale: Solo-maintained and destined for air-gapped industrial environments: fewer dependencies, fewer moving parts, more explicit failure modes.

nodes.label: Mechanical Motion, Dark Only
nodes.rationale: Dark only with no light mode; 120/180/280ms on cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), transform and opacity only, prefers-reduced-motion respected.

nodes.label: No Bare User-Facing Strings In Components
nodes.rationale: Every string goes through src/lib/strings.ts. English only today, but Turkish is the planned second locale and retrofitting extraction later is far more expensive.
nodes.norm_label: no bare user-facing strings in components

nodes.label: Real Content In Examples And Fixtures
nodes.rationale: Plausible part numbers and real dimensions, never 'Part 1 / Part 2' — placeholder fixtures hide the layout and search problems real names cause.
nodes.norm_label: real content in examples and fixtures

nodes.label: Errors Say What Broke And What To Do
nodes.rationale: thiserror in libraries, anyhow at binary edges, no unwrap() outside tests, and a message naming the remedy rather than 'parse failed (3)'.
nodes.norm_label: errors say what broke and what to do

nodes.label: AGENTS.md Rule Mirror
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md's content under the filename every non-Claude agent reads. Generated by `cargo xtask export-agents-md` rather than symlinked, so a Windows checkout without symlink support gets the rules instead of a 9-byte text file; CI fails when the two disagree.

nodes.label: Project Skills Materialized To .agents/skills
nodes.rationale: Skills live in their own repository so a single copy stays current everywhere; `cargo xtask setup` clones them with plain git so an agent with no vendor CLI still gets them.

nodes.label: cargo xtask setup
nodes.rationale: Idempotent first-run command: installs the commit-msg hook (core.hooksPath is local to .git/config so it cannot travel in a commit), reconciles declared plugins, and materializes skills. Every run reports what was already correct, so 'already fine' is distinguishable from 'did not look'.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits, No Length Limit
nodes.rationale: type(scope)!: description with an optional multi-part scope. The rule is about shape, not brevity — this project writes long, precise subjects. Rules and their reasoning live in xtask/src/commit.rs.

nodes.label: No AI Attribution Trailers
nodes.rationale: No Co-Authored-By naming a model or vendor, no ...-Session line, no 'Generated with' footer, for any tool. A message ends at its real content; mentioning a vendor in prose is fine and is not what the check matches.

nodes.label: Verification Bar: fast / verify / slice
nodes.rationale: One command, three tiers, the same gates CI runs — what changes is how often you pay. `fast` (~0.3s, compiles nothing) is the pre-commit hook: fmt, check-layers, check-deploy, check-strings. `verify` adds clippy, tests and staleness gates, skipping cargo-deny and the web suite when nothing they inspect moved. `verify slice` forces both on. Nothing is ever dropped.

nodes.label: Lapidary — Visual Index With A Return Path
nodes.rationale: Not a CAD editor, not a slicer, not a PDM system: the layer that makes parts you already have findable, inspectable and reachable from the tools you already use, with the edit coming back versioned.
nodes.norm_label: lapidary — visual index with a return path

nodes.label: Three Services, Split By Port
nodes.rationale: 3000 web (SPA, proxies /api to api:8080 and nothing else), 8080 api (grid, open path, scan trigger), 8081 worker (the directory walk and everything that touches a file). A route only the worker serves is a route no browser can reach, and the api container mounts no ingest directory to walk.

nodes.label: Scan Enqueues A Job, Never Walks In The Request
nodes.rationale: Both ports accept POST /api/libraries/{id}/scan and neither walks a directory in the request: the route writes one scan_directory job, the worker walks the mount and enqueues one job per model into the same batch, so either port's batch id reports the whole scan. Enqueueing is a database write the api may do; walking a mount and parsing geometry is not.
nodes.norm_label: scan enqueues a job, never walks in the request

nodes.label: Scanning Is Idempotent
nodes.rationale: BLAKE3 is computed before anything else and a hash already in the blob store short-circuits the pipeline — no parse, no raster, no write. A second scan settles every file as skipped, which the grid reports as '6 already here'.

nodes.label: Bundled Example Parts
nodes.rationale: A DN40 flange, module-2 spur gear, vee block, mounting plate, hex spacer and idler pulley, modelled to real dimensions by example/parts/generate.py (stdlib Python, deterministic, watertight) which is committed so the STLs have a source rather than being opaque binaries. First run shows a populated grid rather than an empty one.

nodes.label: SSE Stream Over A One-Second Poll
nodes.rationale: Progress streams over SSE because a browser holds an EventSource open on a hidden document where it will not run a poll. The timer underneath is kept deliberately: the poll makes delivery correct, the stream makes it prompt.
nodes.norm_label: sse stream over a one-second poll

nodes.label: cargo tree Proof That api Does Not Link The Kernel
nodes.rationale: `cargo tree -p lapidary-server | grep lapidary-cad` finds nothing; adding --features mock-kernel finds two lines. One Containerfile builds both images and compose passes SERVER_FEATURES only to worker, so the api container does not merely decline to serve /scan — the code behind it is not linked into the binary.
nodes.norm_label: cargo tree proof that api does not link the kernel

nodes.label: CI rust Job
nodes.rationale: fmt, clippy -D warnings, check-layers, check-deploy, check-strings and the full test suite against a live postgres:18 service pinned by digest.

nodes.label: check-strings Gate
nodes.rationale: Mangled line-continuations inside string literals are invisible to fmt, clippy and every test — fmt does not inspect literal contents — and reach operators as runtime error messages. That class recurred twice, so the gate exists; a gate that runs nowhere closes nothing.

nodes.label: Generated-File Staleness Gate
nodes.rationale: Uses `git status --porcelain`, not `git diff`, because the export deletes and recreates web/src/bindings — a type newly given #[ts(export)] produces an untracked file, and git diff never reports untracked files, so the stalest possible case would pass silently. The same gate covers AGENTS.md and web/src/routeTree.gen.ts.

nodes.label: Commit-Message Backstop Job
nodes.rationale: The local hook is bypassable with --no-verify and absent where setup never ran. Checks only the commits a push or PR adds: 148 commits predate the AI-attribution rule, so a job walking history would fail permanently and teach everyone to ignore it. Skips (saying so) on branch creation, rewritten history, or a range over 20 commits, which means a merge or batch import rather than new work.

nodes.label: cargo-deny CI Job
nodes.rationale: Runs the pinned EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action, enforcing the sources allow-list, licences and the SQL-confinement wrapper rule.

nodes.label: CI web Job
nodes.rationale: npm ci, typecheck, test, build on Node 24, then asserts the committed routeTree.gen.ts matches what the TanStack Router plugin generates.

nodes.label: Containers Workflow
nodes.rationale: Builds lapidary-server, lapidary-web and lapidary-db images on workflow_dispatch or a v* tag only — never on a branch push. It passes no SERVER_FEATURES build arg, so no CI build exercises the mock-kernel path and nothing verifies the built artifacts, only the configuration that would produce them.

nodes.label: Four-Service Compose Stack
nodes.rationale: db, api, worker, web under Compose Spec syntax. No Redis and no broker: the cache and the job queue are both Postgres.

nodes.label: Per-Service Resource Ceilings
nodes.rationale: 1 GiB db, 512 MB api, 2 GiB worker, 256 MB web. Lapidary must run on a modest workstation, not only on a machine with spare gigabytes; the worker gets the largest share because it is the only service that parses meshes, and this ceiling is what makes deferring the L1/L2 rungs a memory decision rather than a latency one.

nodes.label: SERVER_FEATURES Build-Time Image Split
nodes.rationale: One Containerfile builds both images; only worker sets SERVER_FEATURES: mock-kernel, so the api image never links the CAD kernel at all. api logs kernel=none, worker logs kernel=mock. LAPIDARY_ROLE must never be 'api' on the worker — see lapidary-api::Role and ApiError::UnknownRole.

nodes.label: Storage Root As A Bind-Mounted Host Directory
nodes.rationale: A named volume the user cannot locate on disk would defeat the whole point of the browsable layout. Mounted read-write on api too, which is not a hole in the open-path rule: that boundary is a type — SourceStore demands a WorkerRole token lapidary-api cannot obtain — not a mount flag, and a read-only mount would break the derivative cache writes and the upload commit the api legitimately needs.
nodes.norm_label: storage root as a bind-mounted host directory

nodes.label: Uploads Volume Outside The Storage Root
nodes.rationale: Chunks in flight get their own named volume, deliberately not a subdirectory of LAPIDARY_BLOB_ROOT: everything under that root is content-addressed and complete, and a half-transferred file is neither. Persistent on purpose, because the staged file's length is what a resuming upload asks for, so an api restart costs nothing instead of a re-transfer.
nodes.norm_label: uploads volume outside the storage root

nodes.label: Mount The Postgres Parent, Not .../data
nodes.rationale: From PostgreSQL 18 the official image stores data in a major-version-scoped subdirectory, so mounting the old /var/lib/postgresql/data makes the entrypoint hard-fail. Mounting the parent is upstream's recommendation and allows pg_upgrade --link later. Consequence: moving to PG19 is a pg_upgrade job, not a tag change.

nodes.label: Lowercase z, Not Z, On User Directories
nodes.rationale: On an SELinux-enforcing host an unlabelled bind mount gets the worker EACCES on every file. `Z` takes a private per-container label of a directory that belongs to the user and may be open in other programs; `z` applies a shared label, which is what a directory that remains theirs wants. Only lapidary-db is still a named volume.
nodes.norm_label: lowercase z, not z, on user directories

nodes.label: Empty Worker Knobs Mean 'Use The Default'
nodes.rationale: Defaults live in lapidary_jobs::WorkerConfig so exactly one place decides them; restating the numbers in compose would let the two drift. ${VAR:-} yields a present-but-empty variable for every operator who never set one, and an empty string is not a usize — empty_str_as_none in bin/lapidary-server/src/main.rs exists so that case starts the worker instead of refusing to boot.
nodes.norm_label: empty worker knobs mean 'use the default'

nodes.label: Claude Design Handoff Bundle
nodes.rationale: HTML/CSS/JS prototypes exported for a coding agent: recreate them pixel-perfectly in whatever technology fits the target codebase, matching the visual output rather than copying the prototype's internal structure. Read the chat transcripts first — the final HTML is the output, the chat is where the intent lives — and do not screenshot, since dimensions, colours and layout rules are all in the source.

nodes.label: Lapidary Design Prototype (Primary)
nodes.rationale: The design the user had open at handoff. Five screens on a dark #121214 ground with Archivo and JetBrains Mono, a rotated-square cyan mark, a pill search field, a pinned/groups bar and a tag rail above a gallery with grid/cards/list views. Nav is a top bar rather than v1's sidebar.

nodes.label: Library Screen
nodes.rationale: Top nav with centred search, pinned and groups bar, tag rail, then the gallery in three switchable densities: image-first grid tiles, cards, and list.

nodes.label: Model Detail Overlay
nodes.rationale: An overlay rather than a route change, pairing a 3D viewer canvas with a metadata panel — the shape the quick-look and detail page inherit.

nodes.label: Add Model Modal
nodes.rationale: The ingest entry point the empty-state copy was rewritten not to promise until it exists.

nodes.label: Search Suggestions Dropdown
nodes.rationale: The three-class suggestion payload rendered: matching models, creators, and tags, with the header switching between popular tags and suggestions.

nodes.label: Tags And Groups Manager
nodes.rationale: Manages the many-to-many attachments the prototype's domain shape carried as join tables.

nodes.label: Lapidary Design Prototype v1
nodes.rationale: The earliest of the three: a persistent left sidebar plus main column with a topbar, four screens, and 'Tags and collections' rather than groups. No search-suggestions screen and no tag rail — the navigation model the later drafts moved away from.

nodes.label: Lapidary Design Prototype v2 (Mono)
nodes.rationale: Keeps v1's sidebar but adds the search dropdown, a channel rail and image-first grid tiles, in a monochrome treatment. The intermediate step between v1's sidebar and the primary draft's top nav.

nodes.label: One Codebase, Three Artifacts
nodes.rationale: Container stack (Phase 1), the single `lapidary` binary with agent/worker/up (Phase 4), and a Tauri desktop shell (Phase 7) — all thin shells over the same axum Router lapidary-api builds. Never fork.

nodes.label: Podman Leads, Docker Is Supported
nodes.rationale: Docker Desktop requires a paid subscription above 250 employees or $10M revenue, and government entities are excluded from the free tier at any size. The industrial and defence buyers are exactly those cases.

nodes.label: Deployment Topology
nodes.rationale: caddy web in front of axum api, Postgres beside N workers with a native OCCT sidecar, and remote workers taking leases over outbound-only HTTP.

nodes.label: Single Origin Is Mandatory
nodes.rationale: The web container reverse-proxies /api and /events to api, so there is no CORS, no cookie-domain problem and no preflight per request.

nodes.label: SSE Needs proxy_buffering off
nodes.rationale: Default buffering holds progress events until the buffer fills and ingest appears frozen. Needs the Caddy equivalent plus X-Accel-Buffering: no. Named as the single most common works-in-dev-breaks-in-prod bug in this stack.

nodes.label: Version Skew Detection
nodes.rationale: Build every image from the same commit, tag identically, expose /api/version returning the build SHA; the frontend compares against its baked-in value and shows a banner on mismatch.

nodes.label: Three Deployment Modes
nodes.rationale: Server-managed (the enterprise shape, no container runtime on workstations, sidesteps Docker Desktop licensing), local single-user via `lapidary up`, and air-gapped via podman load plus Quadlet units and an offline Ed25519 licence.

nodes.label: Twelve-Crate Modular Monolith
nodes.rationale: Feature isolation enforced by the Cargo dependency graph and a CI check rather than by network boundaries: L0 core, L1 db/storage, L2 feature crates, L3 api/ingest, and an Enterprise wrapper tier.

nodes.label: CI-Enforced Layering Rule
nodes.rationale: L2 crates may depend on L0 and L1 and never on each other or on L3; anything two L2 crates need to share moves to lapidary-core. This is what keeps the monolith from congealing. Enterprise may depend on lapidary-api but never the reverse, because that edge would make the free application depend on the enterprise crate.

nodes.label: FORBIDDEN_PAIRS Named-Pair Prohibitions
nodes.rationale: lapidary-api -> lapidary-cad and lapidary-api -> lapidary-enterprise are forbidden structurally, with check_publish enforcing publish = false on every member, in xtask/src/layers.rs rather than restated in prose. edge_allowed operates on tiers and cannot express a single-pair exception, so a new prohibition extends FORBIDDEN_PAIRS.

nodes.label: lapidary-api Crate
nodes.rationale: L3 library building the axum Router for the open path, grid, health and download. Never lapidary-cad, and never lapidary-storage's SourceStore; it may name SourceReader, the read-only source handle, in download.rs and nowhere else, with cargo xtask check-deploy enforcing both halves.

nodes.label: lapidary-ingest Crate
nodes.rationale: Exists as its own crate rather than a Role::Worker check inside lapidary-api because the images are also split at build time: lapidary-api depending on lapidary-cad at all, even for a route Role::Api never mounts, makes the api image link it regardless. `cargo tree -p lapidary-server -e normal | grep lapidary-cad` is what caught that. The one crate allowed to depend on lapidary-cad and hold a SourceStore.

nodes.label: lapidary-cad Crate
nodes.rationale: L2 crate holding the Kernel trait and the OCCT sidecar driver. Linked only behind the mock-kernel Cargo feature, and only into the worker image.

nodes.label: lapidary-enterprise Crate
nodes.rationale: Licence verification, auth, RBAC, audit and the worker fleet, in a wrapper tier above L3. AGPL like the rest of the workspace — a proprietary crate linking AGPL crates would itself have to be AGPL.

nodes.label: Kernel Trait
nodes.rationale: Container-first deletes the WASM kernel variant entirely — OCCT always runs native in the worker. Keep the trait for test doubles but ship one implementation; this removed the highest-risk item in the original plan. KernelOutput = tessellation L0/L1/L2 glb, structure.json, entities.json.

nodes.label: Kernel Version Pinned Across The Fleet
nodes.rationale: Different OCCT builds produce different tessellations from identical input, and geometric diff depends on determinism. The coordinator must reject leases from workers whose kernel hash does not match the pool's pinned build, or two revisions of an unchanged part show a phantom volume delta depending on which machine processed it.
nodes.norm_label: kernel version pinned across the fleet

nodes.label: Why Not gRPC
nodes.rationale: ts-rs already gives typed contracts from one source; .proto would be a third schema beside SQL and Rust. Blobs must stay on plain HTTP for range requests and immutable caching, so both protocols would run anyway. protoc becomes a build dependency for every contributor, proto3 field presence blurs 'volume is 0.0' from 'volume was never computed', and tonic is not accepting significant new features. Revisit only for a second native plugin; add utoipa/OpenAPI first if a public contract is needed.

nodes.label: Supply Chain Policy
nodes.rationale: cargo-deny with a sources allow-list, not just advisories and licences — without it a transitive dependency can silently come from an arbitrary git URL. Lockfiles committed, Actions pinned to SHAs, cargo vendor for release builds because a regulated customer will ask whether you can build offline and the answer must be demonstrably yes, plus per-release SBOMs and cosign signatures.

nodes.label: No Embedded PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: There is no official embedded PostgreSQL, which is why that path was abandoned. Container mode uses the official postgres:18 Docker Official Image and the problem disappears.

nodes.label: AGPL-3.0-only For The Whole Workspace
nodes.rationale: An AGPL app plus a proprietary enterprise crate conflict: a proprietary crate linking AGPL crates must itself be AGPL, and DCO-signed contributions cannot be relicensed. Decided: everything AGPL, sell the licence contractually — the Ed25519 file gates fleet size and support as a contractual boundary, not technical DRM, and AGPL already blocks a competitor from hosting without publishing changes. A CLA was rejected for the contributor friction it would cost.

nodes.label: Pinned Tech Stack
nodes.rationale: Rust with axum/tokio/sqlx on PostgreSQL 18.6, BLAKE3 not SHA-256 because ingest is hash-bound, object_store with range reads, Postgres FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED plus LISTEN/NOTIFY instead of Redis or a broker, uuid v7 ids. Frontend is React + Vite + TypeScript with no meta-framework, TanStack Router carrying filter state in typed search params, shadcn/ui copied in rather than depended on, and CSS transitions plus the Web Animations API rather than anime.js.

nodes.label: Three Storage Classes, Three Lifecycles
nodes.rationale: Source (never re-derivable, cold), derivative (deterministically re-derivable, warm), preview (cheap, hot). Treating them the same is the most common way this kind of app becomes slow and fat.

nodes.label: Sources Are Path-Addressed, Not Content-Addressed
nodes.rationale: One directory per model named after the part, mirroring the ingest tree, with metadata.json beside the file — the owner wants a folder a user can open in a file manager and find their model by name, not by hash. The cost stated plainly: source deduplication is gone, and it is not recoverable by cleverness, because a store cannot be both one file per model and one file per distinct content.

nodes.label: Content Addressing Survives For blobs/ Only
nodes.rationale: Derivatives only — evictable and rebuildable, never the source of truth. Two-level hex sharding gives 65,536 buckets, keeping any cache directory under ~2k entries at a million derivatives, keyed on BLAKE3.
nodes.norm_label: content addressing survives for blobs/ only

nodes.label: The blobs/ Naming Gap
nodes.rationale: The design called the cache cache/blobs/ and hung a product rule on the name: 'eviction must never read as data loss' is self-evident to anyone opening a directory called cache/. What shipped is blobs/ as a sibling of libraries/ — never-deleted user data and a freely evictable cache side by side, with nothing on disk saying which is which. Recorded rather than argued away; the distinction lives only in UI wording until blob_path changes.

nodes.label: folder.slug Is The Address, folder.name Is The Label
nodes.rationale: Decided 2026-09-07: a rename is a correction to a label, and rewriting every file under WIP because somebody renamed it Archive 2024 is not what that person asked for. If the slug followed the name, slug_path would answer the new directory and the next ingest into that same category would land there — one category, two directories, and another with every rename. PgFolders::rename cannot write a slug; only reslug repoints a category. Scans match by slug, so a renamed library is found rather than forked.
nodes.norm_label: folder.slug is the address, folder.name is the label

nodes.label: Upgrading A Store Created Before This Layout
nodes.rationale: The store moved out of the lapidary-blobs named volume into a bind-mounted host directory and nothing copies it across. Skip the copy and nothing fails at boot — the grid still renders because thumbnails are bytea in Postgres — so the first symptom is a download answering 500, and migrate_storage loops on ENOENT. Nothing is deleted, so it is recoverable after the fact as well as before.
nodes.norm_label: upgrading a store created before this layout

nodes.label: Per-Role Compression With Trained Zstd Dictionaries
nodes.rationale: A pure age rule compresses the derivatives on the hot open path for ~2% space and an added decode stage, so role comes first and age second. A library is hundreds of structurally similar STEP files sharing headers and unit definitions: train per library for 20-40% better ratio. Dictionaries are immutable content-addressed artifacts — losing or mutating one makes blobs unreadable.
nodes.norm_label: per-role compression with trained zstd dictionaries

nodes.label: Nightly Tiering Job
nodes.rationale: Recompresses cold source blobs from -3 to -19, only when idle over 10 minutes, idempotent, resumable, abortable, rate-limited to one core. The atomic rename is the commit point, so a read arriving mid-recompression gets the old blob and nothing ever blocks a read.

nodes.label: Batched Access Tracking
nodes.rationale: An UPDATE per read turns a read-mostly workload into a write-heavy one and leaves a dead tuple per read — a grid scroll touching 300 thumbnails would be 300 writes for zero value. Keep an in-memory map in the API process, flush every 5 minutes in one batched UPDATE, and only write rows over a day stale; day precision is plenty for a 30-day rule.

nodes.label: Eviction Beats Compression, For Derivatives Only
nodes.rationale: Source blobs: compress hard, never delete, ref_count guards removal. Derivatives: never compress, evict freely, since kernel_version plus params_json make regeneration deterministic. The UI wording is a product rule — say render cache, show what it reclaims, and state that source files are untouched.
nodes.norm_label: eviction beats compression, for derivatives only

nodes.label: Thumbnails As bytea In Postgres
nodes.rationale: The deliberate exception to 'no blobs in Postgres': WebP under 64 KB inline on the derivative row so it arrives in the same query as the grid page instead of costing 100 filesystem round trips per scroll. Worth more to perceived speed than any compression decision, and the reason skipping the store upgrade does not break the grid.

nodes.label: Deletion Is Three Steps
nodes.rationale: Delete sets deleted_at and touches no disk; purge is a separate, explicitly worded action refused on a part not deleted first, and recomputes ref_count rather than decrementing because a counter maintained by increments drifts and the thing that acts on the drift deletes bytes; quarantine holds the bytes 30 days. Keep the three apart in every string — wording that lets one read as another is a defect.

nodes.label: Two Quarantines, One Timer
nodes.rationale: blob.quarantined_at is per hash and enters when a recomputed ref_count reaches zero; quarantined_file is per store-relative path and enters when the one part owning that file is purged. Source dedup is gone, so one hash can be several model files with independent lifetimes, which is why the path cannot live on the blob row. Migration 0014 gives both the same 30 days from one constant, because a second retention would be a second promise to explain in the same dialog.

nodes.label: Quarantine Is A Timestamp, Not A quarantine/ Tree
nodes.rationale: The bytes do not move, so restoring needs no path rewrite and no reader needs a second lookup location on the hot path to serve a rare case. What actually keeps a referenced blob safe is neither the counter nor the reaper's WHERE clause but file.blake3 and derivative.blake3 foreign keys; the reachability check merely lets the reaper decline a row rather than fail the whole sweep. Nothing references file.storage_path, so there the check is the only protection.
nodes.norm_label: quarantine is a timestamp, not a quarantine/ tree

nodes.label: LOD Ladder — L0 At Ingest, L1 And L2 On Demand
nodes.rationale: Reverses the earlier 'all generated at ingest' rule on two new facts. Slice 3 measured L0 7.3 MB, L1 41 MB, L2 52 MB over 150 files — 93% of the bytes in rungs the grid never opens; slice 4 writes 7.5 MB, a 92.5% drop. And compose's ceilings say the stack targets a modest workstation, so spending 93 MB per 150 parts on rungs nothing asked for is spending somebody else's disk. L0 still builds at ingest, so the open path still has bytes to paint; if refine reads slow the answer is a background sweep, not three rungs per part.
nodes.norm_label: lod ladder — l0 at ingest, l1 and l2 on demand

nodes.label: meshopt, Not Draco
nodes.rationale: Draco compresses 15-20% smaller but meshopt decodes roughly an order of magnitude faster and is SIMD-friendly, and decode latency dominates for visual triage. Draco is encoded additionally only for the cloud tier where egress bytes cost money.

nodes.label: Immutable Blob Caching
nodes.rationale: /api/blob/{blake3} can never return different bytes, so max-age=31536000, immutable, an ETag of the hash and range support come free from content addressing — repeat opens hit the browser cache with no round trip and no invalidation logic. But every blob request must still verify the principal reaches a part referencing it.

nodes.label: Prefetch On Intent
nodes.rationale: Hover a card prefetches L0; opening the inspector prefetches L1 for the neighbours in sort order. Bound the pool at 2 and cancel on navigate, or fast scrolling saturates the queue with parts already passed.

nodes.label: Performance Targets As Regression Tests
nodes.rationale: Grid page of 100 under 80 ms warm, part open to first paint under 120 ms, open to L2 under 600 ms, search over 100k parts under 150 ms, facet counts under 300 ms. Treated as tests, not aspirations.

nodes.label: Five Extraction Stages, Each Committing Independently
nodes.rationale: Identity (always succeeds, and a known hash short-circuits everything), structural, geometric, semantic, derived. A stage-4 failure still leaves a usable, searchable part.
nodes.norm_label: five extraction stages, each committing independently

nodes.label: Columns vs JSONB — One Rule
nodes.rationale: If it appears in a filter, sort or facet it is a typed column with an index; everything else is JSONB. ORDER BY (metadata->>'volume')::float is unindexable in practice and becomes a seq scan at ~50k rows.

nodes.label: Core Schema
nodes.rationale: part / revision / file / blob / derivative / part_source / part_image, on uuid v7 with a STORED tsvector. Two deviations from the sketch are built and deliberate: position rather than is_primary on part_image, because a part carries an ordered gallery a boolean could not express, and bytes inline or in a blob at the same 64 KB line, so the store has one rule about small images rather than two.

nodes.label: Dual Index: tsvector Plus pg_trgm
nodes.rationale: to_tsvector('english','A1234-56-B') mangles identifiers, so searching 1234 will not find it — this bites every parts application eventually. Run both indexes, union, and rank trigram similarity above text rank when the query looks like an identifier. Turkish needs a language column on library, because the tsvector config is fixed at index time.

nodes.label: 10k Exact-Count Facet Threshold
nodes.rationale: Under 10k matching rows, exact counts in one query with FILTER aggregates; above that, a rollup or no counts at all. Users tolerate missing counts; they do not tolerate a 900 ms filter panel.

nodes.label: Custom Fields, Max 8 Indexed
nodes.rationale: Values live in part.metadata_json with a matching expression index when indexed. Capped at 8 because each is a write cost on every ingest.

nodes.label: Non-Destructive Image Framing
nodes.rationale: fit, focus_x and focus_y are CSS object-fit and object-position applied by the browser at display time, so the stored WebP is never re-encoded and adjusting the framing is free, reversible, and costs no generation of quality.

nodes.label: Do Not Build A Scraper
nodes.rationale: Three source-link paths in order — upload, paste an image URL (fetch once, store as a blob, never hotlink because hosts rotate URLs and hotlinking leaks a referrer on every grid scroll), and an explicit OpenGraph fetch button. Systematic harvesting breaks on every redesign and violates GrabCAD and TraceParts ToS specifically.

nodes.label: Fetching A User-Supplied URL Is SSRF
nodes.rationale: Resolve DNS first and check the resolved IP against RFC1918, loopback, link-local (169.254.169.254 especially), ULA and mapped-v4, re-checking after every redirect for DNS rebinding. http/https only, 3 redirects, 10 s, 10 MB enforced while streaming, content-type and magic bytes, explicit image::Limits because a 200 KB PNG can declare 50000x50000 and take the process out. Re-encoding to bounded WebP normalizes, mitigates bombs and strips EXIF GPS in one step.
nodes.norm_label: fetching a user-supplied url is ssrf

nodes.label: Download variant=original, Re-Hashed Before Serving
nodes.rationale: original is the only legal value today; variant=3mf is a 400 naming what to send, never a silent fallback. The route re-hashes the bytes and refuses with 500 on mismatch, which is what makes 'verifiable against the stored BLAKE3' true rather than asserted, at microseconds against the transfer. Cache-Control: no-cache, because this URL names a revision whose source could be re-pointed, unlike the blob route whose URL contains the hash. RFC 5987 filenames, because Turkish part names contain g-breve, s-cedilla and dotless i.

nodes.label: Hash First, Client-Side, Then Probe
nodes.rationale: BLAKE3 in WASM before uploading, then POST /api/uploads/probe returns have/need so 480 of 500 dragged files never transfer. Resumable chunked upload is mandatory — a 2 GB STEP over a corporate VPN as one POST will fail at 90% — and the server verifies the assembled hash against the client's claim, because it is the dedup key and a wrong one silently corrupts another user's part.

nodes.label: Streaming ZIP Bundles, STORE Not DEFLATE
nodes.rationale: Never buffered server-side; contents are already compressed so deflating again burns CPU for nothing. manifest.json with part numbers, revisions, hashes and source licences makes the bundle verifiable rather than a folder of mystery files.
nodes.norm_label: streaming zip bundles, store not deflate

nodes.label: Archive Security
nodes.rationale: 3MF is a ZIP and therefore a zip-bomb vector: cap decompressed size, entry count and compression ratio during extraction and abort on breach, not after. Reject absolute paths and .. segments — old, still exploited.

nodes.label: Geometric Diff Replaces Textual Diff
nodes.rationale: Delta volume, bbox per axis, mass and centre of mass, triangle/face/edge counts, plus an overlay with the old as a grey ghost. Per-face Hausdorff is the premium version: expensive, async, cached, and never in the synchronous diff path.

nodes.label: External Round-Trip Watcher Rules
nodes.rationale: Checkout to a flat human-readable workspace folder because users open it in a file manager. Debounce 500 ms then wait for write-settle; ignore editor scratch files; hash before believing anything, since editors touch mtime constantly without changing content and identical bytes are not a revision. Windows ReadDirectoryChangesW overflows a fixed kernel buffer during bulk operations and silently drops events, so handle overflow with a full rescan; macOS FSEvents coalesces at directory granularity. inotify does not propagate through Docker Desktop bind mounts on macOS or Windows, which is why the watcher lives in the native agent binary.

nodes.label: Be Honest About Which Tools Round-Trip
nodes.rationale: Rhino, FreeCAD, Blender, SolidWorks and the slicers write back the file we handed them; Fusion 360 and Onshape cannot, being cloud-backed. For those the honest flow is export-and-reimport and the UI must say so — overpromising destroys trust in version history, which is the feature everything else hangs on.
nodes.norm_label: be honest about which tools round-trip

nodes.label: Feature List With Phase Tags And Explicit Non-Goals
nodes.rationale: Items marked [—] are deliberate non-goals, not oversights: merge/branches/textual diff, direct-to-printer sending, geometry editing ever, catalogue scraping, full MRP, per-widget polling (a self-inflicted DoS), and phone-home licence checks.
nodes.norm_label: feature list with phase tags and explicit non-goals

nodes.label: Move History: Route Only, Deliberately Unread
nodes.rationale: GET /api/parts/{id}/moves shipped and answers correctly, but nothing displays it — a product call taken 2026-09-07, not an oversight: a 'moved from' line is history about a thing whose current location the card already shows. Its [] answer for an unknown part id is the same as 'never moved', deliberately, because nothing acts differently on the two.
nodes.norm_label: move history: route only, deliberately unread

nodes.label: Page Size And Density Per Viewer, Per Library
nodes.rationale: 'Per library' would have meant a column, but with no user table, session table or auth in Phase 1 a column makes one operator's choice everybody's — and is wrong the moment auth arrives. Stored in the browser keyed by library id: each library remembers its own setting, and the memory is that browser's.
nodes.norm_label: page size and density per viewer, per library

nodes.label: Licence On The Detail Page, Not The Grid Card
nodes.rationale: Half of hobbyist STL libraries are non-commercial and somebody selling prints needs to see CC-BY-NC first, but the grid query is at its 16-column FromRow ceiling and reworking that tuple to put a sentence on a tile someone is scanning at a glance is the wrong trade. It is one click away, in the quick-look, which is where the decision to print is actually made.
nodes.norm_label: licence on the detail page, not the grid card

nodes.label: OpenGraph Fetching Is Out
nodes.rationale: Owner decision. part_image.origin still carries og_fetched so adding it later stays additive, and DATA.md is emphatic about where that road ends.

nodes.label: Source Links And Images Pulled Forward To Phase 1
nodes.rationale: Owner decision, 2026-09-07: a part with a photograph and a link to where it came from is most of what makes a library worth sitting in front of, and none of it depends on anything Phase 2 onwards adds.
nodes.norm_label: source links and images pulled forward to phase 1

nodes.label: Build Graph (Blueprint Board) Spec
nodes.rationale: The largest subsystem, comparable in size to everything before it. process_type, build_graph, build_graph_revision, build_node, build_edge, build_step, build_run and build_run_node.

nodes.label: Two Graphs, Not One: BOM Tree vs Process Graph
nodes.rationale: A BOM answers what it is made of and changes with the design; a process graph answers how to make it and changes with the method. The same BOM has different process graphs for FDM versus injection moulding — exactly the hobbyist/industrial overlap — and it only works if they are separate objects. Conflating them is what makes assembly tools unusable.
nodes.norm_label: two graphs, not one: bom tree vs process graph

nodes.label: ~15 Builtin Process Types With JSON Schema Params
nodes.rationale: Printing needs printer/material/layer height, moulding needs tool number/shot weight/cycle time/cavities. A free-text tag loses all of it; a fixed enum locks out workflows we did not predict — hence a schema per type plus user-defined types, with the palette filtered by library so a hobbyist does not scroll past injection moulding to find FDM.
nodes.norm_label: ~15 builtin process types with json schema params

nodes.label: Runs Are Instances, Graphs Are Templates
nodes.rationale: Without the split you cannot build the same assembly twice, cannot track two units in parallel, and editing a graph destroys the history of what was already built.
nodes.norm_label: runs are instances, graphs are templates

nodes.label: Pinned vs Floating Node Revisions
nodes.rationale: A node with revision_id null silently changes what gets built when someone uploads a new revision. Support both, show the difference clearly, default to pinned in controlled libraries and floating in hobby ones.

nodes.label: Ready-Set Ordering
nodes.rationale: Critical path first, then batch affinity (five ready parts in the same filament is one plate, not five), then shortest first so progress feels visible — that ordering is what makes it useful rather than merely correct. Quantities multiply through the graph, seeded by build_run.qty: MRP-lite, and it must stay that way. Cycles are rejected at write time via petgraph, returning which edge closed the loop, because a cycle in the database makes the ready-set query loop forever.

nodes.label: Two UIs On The Same Data: Board And Guide
nodes.rationale: The board designs the process at a desk and writes build_graph; the guide follows it on a phone at the bench and writes build_run_node. The guide is a linearization of the DAG using the ready-set ranking, but any ready step may be marked done out of order, because no real shop works strictly sequentially. Auto-generate the first draft from each process type's template: nobody writes forty steps from a blank page, and a guide that starts empty stays empty.
nodes.norm_label: two uis on the same data: board and guide

nodes.label: Documentation Map
nodes.rationale: Says which doc to read before which kind of work. The docs describe the system; superpowers/ describes particular pieces of work on it — a spec is authoritative for its own slice and silent about everything else, and a plan is a record of intent at a moment rather than of what shipped. Where a spec and the code disagree, one of them is a defect: say which, in the spec.

nodes.label: Skills Are Declared, Not Vendored
nodes.rationale: Copying them into .claude/skills/ forked them from their upstream repository — edit one and the other silently stops matching, on every machine independently. .claude/settings.json declares plugins and marketplaces; .agents/skills/ is a gitignored materialized cache, because committing it would fork the skills again.

nodes.label: Things That Look Like Bugs But Are Decisions
nodes.rationale: STORED generated columns, batched last_accessed_at, STORE-not-DEFLATE bundles, thumbnails as bytea with no images/ directory and no config file in the store, quarantined_at as a column with nothing behind it yet, and the watcher living in the native agent. One entry is admitted as a gap rather than a decision: the derivative cache is blobs/, a sibling of libraries/, not cache/blobs/ as the slice spec drew it.
nodes.norm_label: things that look like bugs but are decisions

nodes.label: Phase 0 — Foundation
nodes.rationale: Container-first removed the OCCT bundling gate, so this is no longer a go/no-go risk. Exit: podman compose up on a clean machine serves a page and occt-bridge converts a 200-part STEP assembly in under 30 s. Verify pgvector and the Turkish snowball config here, not later.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Ingest And Grid
nodes.rationale: Blob CAS, the Postgres job queue, mesh ingest to thumbnail plus L0, virtualized grid, SSE progress, download original, and a bundled licence-clean example part so the first grid is never empty.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Exit Measurement, 2026-09-07
nodes.rationale: 1,095 real STLs / 15.67 GB in 130.3 s; re-drop 40.1 s with 0 re-ingested; grid 5.3 ms median at page size 50. The fourth clause failed: one 635,470-triangle file clustered to nothing and MeshKernel::process used ?, so an unmakeable derivative was indistinguishable from an unreadable file and no part row was written. Fixed so parsing stays fatal but a failed derivative lands in KernelOutput::unproduced. The measurement also corrected its own diagnosis — CadError::Unrenderable is raised by both the rasterizer and the glTF writer, so a tessellation_l0 failure was written up as a thumbnail failure.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — CAD Ingest And Search
nodes.rationale: STEP and IGES through the sidecar, extraction stages 1-4, dual search and facets. Exit: a mixed folder ingests with no manual steps and the fragment 1234 returns A1234-56-B at position one.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Viewer And Measurement
nodes.rationale: Exit: measure a known cylinder from STEP and get the exact nominal diameter, not a tessellated approximation, with part open to first paint under 120 ms warm.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Versioning, Agent, Round-Trip
nodes.rationale: This phase is the differentiator; everything before it is a file browser. Exit: open a STEP in FreeCAD, change it, save, and a new revision appears with a correct volume delta on Linux, macOS and Windows. Three-step deletion landed early in Phase 1 slice 7 on the owner's call — a library you could add to and never remove from was the more pressing gap — leaving tiering here, because tiering is what makes quarantine's physical layout matter.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — Source Links, Bundles, Collections
nodes.rationale: Exit: paste a Printables URL and get title, licence and a cached image; export a 40-part assembly another user can import with lineage intact.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — Dashboard And Similarity
nodes.rationale: Exit: a 12-widget dashboard settles in one round trip and uploading a known part surfaces its near-duplicates.

nodes.label: Phase 7 — Build Graph
nodes.rationale: Do not start early: a half-working planner attached to a good browser makes the whole app feel unfinished. Exit: a three-level assembly, a run of 4 units, correct quantities in the queue, followed to completion on a phone.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Enterprise And Fleet
nodes.rationale: Exit: register three remote workers, process a 500-part library across the fleet, revoke one mid-run and watch its leases expire and requeue cleanly.

nodes.label: Phase 9 — Cloud
nodes.rationale: Only after the local product has users. Zero-egress object storage on day one, not as an optimization; per-tenant dedup only, never cross-tenant; egress instrumented per tenant from the first beta day; a lapsed subscription goes read-only with full download, never deletion.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Tauri Shell
nodes.rationale: Three connection modes, embedded never built. Bundles only our own binaries — if you are tempted to bundle Postgres or OCCT, stop.

nodes.label: Meter Per Worker Node, Not Per Seat
nodes.rationale: Distributed compute is inherently multi-machine, so a hobbyist on one laptop loses nothing while a shop with eight workstations gets real value — near-perfect price/value alignment with zero crippling of the free app. Seats are annoying to administer, easy to fudge and resented; worker count is a hard number the coordinator already knows and drops into max_workers in an offline signed licence. Grace period, never a hard stop: a customer whose line halts over a lapsed licence will not renew, and will tell people.
nodes.norm_label: meter per worker node, not per seat

nodes.label: Two Payment Rails, Both Required
nodes.rationale: MoR for cloud and small card purchases, and invoice plus purchase order plus e-fatura plus wire — a EUR 5,000 self-hosted licence does not go through a checkout page. That second rail is where the highest-value customers live and is the one solo developers forget to build.

nodes.label: Law 4691 Technology Development Zone Exemption
nodes.rationale: Erciyes Teknopark earnings from in-zone software and R&D are exempt from income and corporate tax until 31/12/2028 with matching VAT relief. Conditions are strict (munhasiran, management-company approval, a qualified-expenditure ratio, a 2% VC contribution above 1M TL). Plausibly worth more in year one than any pricing decision, and some of it depends on day-one entity structure — take it to a mali musavir before incorporating.

nodes.label: Roadmap Open Items
nodes.rationale: Trademark clearance for a common English word, pgvector and Turkish tsvector against postgres:18, measuring the zstd dictionary gain on a real STEP corpus before committing, MoR Turkey payout support, and WebKitGTK variance across Linux distros.

nodes.label: Prototype Domain Shape That Survived
nodes.rationale: model.service.ts settled on identity, classification, geometry, provenance and derivative-presence flags, with tags, groups and printer types as join tables resolved to sorted name lists. Lapidary keeps the shape and moves the join resolution behind repository traits. The bug not carried forward: listModels did SELECT * and filtered in TypeScript.

nodes.label: Three-Class Search Payload
nodes.rationale: One query returned matching models, creators with counts, and tags from matched models, with the header switching between POPULAR TAGS and TAGS & SUGGESTIONS. Tag counts came from a full GROUP BY on every keystroke, which tsvector plus pg_trgm and the 10k threshold replace — but the shape of the suggestion payload is right.

nodes.label: ingestMesh Ordering And Two Callers
nodes.rationale: The ingest primitive, called from the bulk folder scan and from the multipart upload branch. Tier 3 (compressed original) always first and unguarded, then Tier 2 (LOD plus metrics) through a 60 s sidecar; the thumbnail tier was explicitly out of scope and arrived later via its own route. The two callers diverge after it returns, and the divergence is not cosmetic.

nodes.label: The Prototype Never Hashed Anything
nodes.rationale: Grepping the four ingest services for hash|blake|sha256|checksum returns nothing — a direct divergence from 'hash first, always', not a variant of it. Duplicate detection happened a layer up by filename, and only on the scan path; the upload path had none. modelId was a fresh nanoid per call, never derived from content, so nothing was idempotent or resumable: identity must come from the content hash so a retried ingest is naturally recognized rather than accidentally re-run.

nodes.label: Orphaned Blob Leak On DB Failure
nodes.rationale: If ingestMesh wrote a blob and the following createModel threw, the scan path only incremented `skipped` and never unlinked it; the upload path had no catch at all, so it leaked and 500'd. Neither had a reaper. Blob writes need reconciling with the DB write — staged blob plus transactional commit, or an explicit reaper — because silent leaks are what 'we never delete user data implicitly' was written against, and never reclaiming orphaned data is just as much a problem to design out.
nodes.norm_label: orphaned blob leak on db failure

nodes.label: Measured And User-Typed Dimensions Shared Columns
nodes.rationale: The upload route wrote user-typed numbers into the same bbox_x/y/z columns a sidecar measurement fills, with no provenance marker. Either persist a provenance tag alongside every dimension triple or refuse to let a typed dimension land in measured columns at all — emphatically must not survive into Phase 1 in any form.
nodes.norm_label: measured and user-typed dimensions shared columns

nodes.label: Vertex Clustering LOD On A 48-Cubed Grid
nodes.rationale: rust-mesh was dependency-free so it compiled offline in the container build — a constraint worth preserving. Vertex clustering is the right first LOD algorithm: single pass, no topology required, degrades gracefully on the malformed meshes real libraries contain. The 48 constant was tuned by eye and should become an L0/L1/L2 ladder.
nodes.norm_label: vertex clustering lod on a 48-cubed grid

nodes.label: Library Scan And The Debounce That Never Existed
nodes.rationale: A recursive synchronous walk-then-ingest pass bounded to 3 concurrent tasks, deduping by filename stem, with no watcher and no debounce at all — recording the absence is a real finding, not padding. Keep bounded concurrency and scan-as-an-explicit-action, which matches 'nothing happens implicitly'. Discard filename-stem dedup so same-named files in different folders do not silently lose one to unsorted walk order, and surface walk errors instead of letting them vanish.
nodes.norm_label: library scan and the debounce that never existed

nodes.label: Slicer Profile Parsing And The Curated Key Map
nodes.rationale: PrusaSlicer/Orca/SuperSlicer .ini and .json, chosen purely by extension. Section headers were recognized only well enough to be skipped, never tracked, so identically-named keys in different sections silently collide and the later one wins; no inheritance was implemented. The curated key map is the hard-won part and is the seed for lapidary-targets — captured before that work starts.
nodes.norm_label: slicer profile parsing and the curated key map

nodes.label: Explicitly Not Carried Forward
nodes.rationale: cache.service.ts and its Redis — the cache and the job queue are both Postgres; per-model procedural sample shapes in seed.ts, replaced by one real licence-clean example part; and `npm run dev` as the primary run path, replaced by podman compose up.

nodes.label: Phase 0a Foundation Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Twelve tasks replacing the deleted Node prototype with a Rust workspace, a TanStack SPA and a four-service stack that serves a health-checked page, with the layering rule in CI from the first commit. Names superpowers:subagent-driven-development as the required sub-skill.

nodes.label: Plan Global Constraints
nodes.rationale: Restates the project rules as per-task requirements: no SQL outside lapidary-db enforced by deny.toml wrappers, lapidary-api never gaining a main.rs, no unwrap() outside tests via #![deny(clippy::unwrap_used)], anyhow only in bin/ and xtask/, dark-only frontend, every string through strings.ts, STORED generated columns, and cargo fmt before every Rust commit since the plan's code blocks are written for readability rather than rustfmt output.

nodes.label: Pinned Version Table And Split Pinning Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Cargo.toml uses ordinary caret requirements with Cargo.lock as the pin — idiomatic Cargo and what cargo deny checks — while package.json uses exact versions with no caret and commits package-lock.json, because npm's resolution is looser. Each internal path dependency carries an explicit version, or cargo records it as * and deny.toml's wildcards=deny rejects every crate-to-crate edge in the workspace.
nodes.norm_label: pinned version table and split pinning mechanism

nodes.label: Plan File Structure Table
nodes.rationale: Path-by-responsibility map: newtype ids and Approximate<T> in lapidary-core, repository traits as the only crate that may name sqlx, the Kernel trait and MockKernel, router() as a library, xtask/src/layers.rs holding the rule pure and unit-testable, and web/src/bindings committed so CI can detect staleness.

nodes.label: Task 3: xtask check-layers
nodes.rationale: A custom xtask parsing cargo metadata to enforce the tier rule, written as a pure unit-testable function so the rule itself can be tested rather than only observed in CI.

nodes.label: Task 5: Kernel Trait And MockKernel
nodes.rationale: An in-process MockKernel behind the trait; the real OCCT sidecar is Phase 0b and nothing in this plan depends on it.

nodes.label: Task 8: ts-rs Export Pipeline
nodes.rationale: One source of truth for wire types. uuid-impl and jiff-impl are not optional extras — without them ts-rs has no TS impl for Uuid or jiff::Timestamp and lapidary-core does not compile.

nodes.label: Task 10: Container Images And The Compose Stack
nodes.rationale: Rust multi-stage to lapidary-server, postgres:18 plus pgvector, node build to caddy static serve, and a four-service compose file with no Redis and no broker. OCCT is Phase 0b and deliberately absent.
nodes.norm_label: task 10: container images and the compose stack

nodes.label: Task 11: CI And Supply Chain
nodes.rationale: AGPL-3.0-only, not the bare deprecated AGPL-3.0 id, or cargo-deny rejects all fourteen of our own crates while passing every third-party one. The sqlx wrapper list confines SQL to lapidary-db; lapidary-api appears only because #[sqlx::test] is a dev-dependency, and if that list grows further, SQL has leaked.

nodes.label: Task 12: Exit-Criteria Verification
nodes.rationale: Eight checks, including proving the layering check fails on an injected violation rather than only passing, verifying pgvector and the Turkish config, confirming bindings and the route tree track their sources, checking the LICENSE file agrees with the prose around it, and running under Docker as well as Podman with both ignore files present or the context is the whole repo.

nodes.label: Phase 0a Follow-Ups Ledger
nodes.rationale: Everything found, judged and deliberately not done in Phase 0a, each item saying what it is, why it was left and what it costs to leave. Two execution passes on 2026-09-02 closed most of the self-contained subset; anything not marked Closed is still open.

nodes.label: Promoting lapidary-enterprise Out Of L3
nodes.rationale: The layering rule used to permit L3 to L3, so lapidary-api to lapidary-enterprise passed CI — an edge that would make the free application depend on the enterprise crate. Closed by giving enterprise its own tier: the edge is now rejected structurally with a violation message naming the product rule it protects, while enterprise to api stays legal.

nodes.label: FORBIDDEN_PAIRS Replaces A Comment
nodes.rationale: Removing the api-to-cad dependency left only a comment asserting the invariant, because edge_allowed(L3,L2) returned true unconditionally. A (from,to,why) triple list checked beside the tier rule now fails the edge structurally while leaving a different L3-to-L2 edge legal — a named pair, not a blanket ban. Proven to bite by adding the dependency back and watching the check fail. This is the mechanism for future prohibitions; edge_allowed operates on tiers and cannot express a single-pair exception.

nodes.label: SERVER_FEATURES As A Build Arg
nodes.rationale: Both services once built from the same Containerfile with --features mock-kernel hardcoded, so the binary serving the open path linked the kernel crate. The feature list became a build arg declared inside the build stage — a bare ARG before FROM would have been the wrong scope — set only by worker. Verified by reading each image's startup kernel line. Not the same as splitting the binary by role, which stays the real fix.

nodes.label: cargo xtask check-deploy
nodes.rationale: Checks that exactly the services in KERNEL_LINKED_SERVICES set SERVER_FEATURES, that the Containerfile's cargo build routes through the expansion rather than a hardcoded flag, and that ARG SERVER_FEATURES is visible to that build line across every stage. A fourth violation class catches the parser itself going stale, naming the function to fix rather than blaming the config. The check is static — it reads text, does not build an image, and its own failure message says so.

nodes.label: publish = false Enforced By check_publish
nodes.rationale: Setting publish = false on all 13 manifests let deny.toml use allow-wildcard-paths instead of a version pin on every internal path dependency, removing the coupling that required editing eleven lines on a version bump — but only a comment tied the two together, so a new crate would silently inherit the exemption. check_publish now fails any member whose cargo metadata publish field is not null, saying what to add and why.

nodes.label: Open: worker And api Are The Same Process
nodes.rationale: Correct for 0a's prove-the-topology goal, but Phase 1 needs a LAPIDARY_ROLE switch or a subcommand before the worker leases jobs, or the queue is served by two full HTTP routers and lapidary-server's 'api plus optionally in-process worker' description stays fiction. Splitting the images removed the kernel from the open-path artifact but did not give the worker its own identity.
nodes.norm_label: open: worker and api are the same process

nodes.label: Open: The Source-File Half Of The Open-Path Rule
nodes.rationale: The kernel half is closed twice over, but lapidary-api still depends on lapidary-storage, so nothing structural stops an open-path handler reading source bytes. A FORBIDDEN_PAIRS entry cannot express it: the crates must stay connected for derivatives, and the distinction is which bytes a handler reads, not whether the crates may be connected — a dependency-graph check only sees the latter. Needs an API-level boundary, such as a derivatives-only handle open-path handlers can hold and a source-reading one they cannot.
nodes.norm_label: open: the source-file half of the open-path rule

nodes.label: Open: KernelOutput Will Have To Change
nodes.rationale: Phase 0b needs blob references for the LOD ladder, and measurement cannot snap to opaque strings like 'CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE:22.000' — it needs axes, radii and normals. The change is cheap now, since mock.rs plus four tests are the only construction sites, and the mesh-yields-no-analytic-entities invariant survives any richer entity type. Only the sidecar README's false claim that the trait does not change was corrected; the redesign itself is open.
nodes.norm_label: open: kerneloutput will have to change

nodes.label: Open: Secrets Visible To docker inspect
nodes.rationale: Compose interpolates POSTGRES_PASSWORD into DATABASE_URL for api and worker, so the plaintext password is readable by anyone with engine access. Standard for compose without a secrets backend and not baked into an image layer; revisit with podman/docker secrets or an external manager when the fleet story lands.
nodes.norm_label: open: secrets visible to docker inspect

nodes.label: Classifying Connect Failures By SQLSTATE
nodes.rationale: Every connect() failure used to map to Unreachable, so a wrong password read as 'could not reach the database'. Now classified into AuthenticationFailed, DatabaseMissing and Unreachable, each carrying only a redacted target, with a regression test asserting no rendered message leaks credentials.

nodes.label: Empty-State Copy Promised An Interaction That Did Not Exist
nodes.rationale: 'Drop a folder of STL or STEP files to begin' was untrue — nothing implemented dropping a folder. Reworded to something true today, with a regression test asserting the component renders the string so its use cannot drift silently. The ingest half stays open: Phase 1 shipping ingest and restoring a truthful call to action is an acceptance item.
nodes.norm_label: empty-state copy promised an interaction that did not exist

nodes.label: Phase 0a Exit-Criteria Verification
nodes.rationale: Run from a fresh clone of rust-rewrite at 8bbe1f8 rather than the working tree, so the report describes what a new machine sees. 8 of 8 criteria PASS. CI execution is explicitly out of scope because the branch is deliberately unpushed and the task was told not to push.

nodes.label: cargo xtask check-layers
nodes.rationale: Enforces docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's rule that L2 crates may depend only on L0 and L1, never on each other or on L3. Verified by injecting lapidary-vcs -> lapidary-index, watching it exit 1 naming the edge and the remedy, then reverting to a clean pass over 14 workspace crates.

nodes.label: Prove the Check Bites
nodes.rationale: A check is only verified by deliberately breaking what it guards, confirming a non-zero exit naming that specific problem, then reverting and confirming a clean pass. Asserting that a check passes proves nothing about whether it still checks anything; this repo has repeatedly found checks that silently stopped checking.

nodes.label: Supply-Chain Gate
nodes.rationale: cargo deny check green, both lockfiles committed, and every workflow `uses:` carrying a 40-hex commit SHA. Nine duplicate-crate warnings from sqlx pulling block-buffer/digest at two semver-majors are non-fatal and expected. Whether the workflows execute on GitHub was not verified — that needs a push.

nodes.label: Container Engine Parity
nodes.rationale: The stack builds and serves /api/healthz under both podman and docker, and .containerignore/.dockerignore pairs are byte-identical or the build context is the whole repo. Scope note recorded honestly: rootless podman delegates to the docker-compose CLI plugin, so this exercises two engines but one compose implementation.

nodes.label: Generated-Artifact Staleness Check
nodes.rationale: Regenerate ts-rs bindings and the TanStack route tree in a clean clone with npm ci (never npm install, so no local node_modules interference), then `git diff --exit-code` them. A zero diff is the only proof the checked-in generated files still track the Rust types and the routes.

nodes.label: Item 15 — Worker-Only Kernel Invariant in CI
nodes.rationale: Item 13 created a sibling invariant to item 12's and left it enforced by a comment and nothing else. Three edits that would break it all pass CI today. Half of item 15 stays open deliberately: building images in CI would pre-empt item 4's role split, and the check must not decide that design as a side effect.
nodes.norm_label: item 15 — worker-only kernel invariant in ci

nodes.label: cargo xtask check-deploy
nodes.rationale: An xtask subcommand rather than a grep step in ci.yml: a shell grep is three lines but untested, CI-only, and unrunnable locally before a push. Parses deploy/compose.yaml and deploy/Containerfile line-wise — no serde_yaml, which is unmaintained and would trip cargo deny advisories. The check is static: it verifies the configuration that would produce the right images, never the images.

nodes.label: Worker-Only Kernel Linking Invariant
nodes.rationale: Only the worker image links the CAD kernel, because the open path never invokes it. Expressed as a named list of kernel-linked services written generically over all service blocks, so a future api-replica is covered without anyone remembering to add it, plus the requirement that ARG SERVER_FEATURES is declared after the first FROM — an ARG before it is a different scope and would silently ship a worker with no kernel.

nodes.label: Parse-Stale Violation
nodes.rationale: A line-wise parser that cannot find what it expects must fail loudly, not pass silently — and its message must say the check's parsing is stale, not that the config is wrong. The two failures need opposite fixes and a check reporting the wrong one sends the reader to the wrong file. Written because a previous round shipped an assertion whose two halves could both degrade to an empty string, compare equal, and pass having verified nothing.

nodes.label: Phase 0a Follow-Ups — Execution Plan
nodes.rationale: Executes only the follow-ups that are self-contained and verifiable today; everything else stays on the standing to-do list with its reason intact. Deferrals are argued rather than listed: Approximate<T>'s first real consumer in Phase 3 decides its shape, and guessing now bakes in the wrong one.

nodes.label: Enterprise Layer
nodes.rationale: A layer variant above L3 holding lapidary-enterprise alone, named Enterprise rather than L4 because it is a wrapper tier existing for one product reason, not a fifth peer. L3 may not depend on it, protecting 'the application is free and complete'. Both crates were empty, so the change cost nothing then and gets more expensive with every file added.

nodes.label: Id Newtypes
nodes.rationale: LibraryId, PartId and RevisionId gain from_uuid and FromStr but deliberately not From<Uuid>: three distinct id types converting implicitly from one Uuid is exactly how a PartId ends up where a LibraryId belongs. lapidary-core may not depend on sqlx, so any Uuid-to-newtype query glue belongs in lapidary-db.

nodes.label: mock-kernel feature
nodes.rationale: The worker binary depends on lapidary-cad directly rather than through a feature chain via lapidary-api — the only option compatible with dropping the unused api -> cad edge, and it keeps the kernel out of the crate serving the open path. A startup log line reporting the linked kernel is a deliberate minimal real use; an unused optional dependency would repeat the mistake being removed.

nodes.label: publish = false
nodes.rationale: Internal path dependencies carried version = "0.1.0" only to satisfy deny.toml's wildcards = "deny", coupling eleven lines to the workspace version. publish = false on every application crate removes the coupling and prevents an accidental cargo publish of an AGPL app crate; allow-wildcard-paths = true is safe precisely because of it, and the two changes must never be separated.

nodes.label: Database Error Classification
nodes.rationale: connect() mapped every failure to DbError::Unreachable, so a wrong password told the operator to check a service that was running fine. SQLSTATE 28P01/28000 become AuthenticationFailed, 3D000 becomes DatabaseMissing, and Unreachable stays the fallback for genuine IO/DNS/timeout. Routed through a private function over &sqlx::Error so it is unit-testable without a live server.

nodes.label: redact_credentials
nodes.rationale: The only thing that may put a URL in an error message. Every new error variant must be covered by the regression test that classifies an error carrying postgres://lapidary:sup3rs3cret@db:5432/lapidary and asserts no rendered message contains the password — not just the variants that existed when the leak was found.

nodes.label: Prototype Knowledge Capture
nodes.rationale: Three of seven areas the spec required before deleting the Node prototype were missed: assetPipeline/meshSidecar ingest ordering, libraryScan's walk and debounce, and profileImport slicer profile parsing. Recoverable from origin/main, so not urgent — but slicer profile parsing is hard-won and heads for lapidary-targets, so capture it before that work starts. A finding that an area was thinner than claimed is a useful result, not a failure.

nodes.label: Phase 0a Follow-Ups Round 2
nodes.rationale: Closes the four items the first pass created or made cheap. cargo fmt --all --check is listed first in the verification bar deliberately: the previous pass shipped a formatting violation that survived its own review and five later verification passes because no bar named it.

nodes.label: FORBIDDEN_PAIRS
nodes.rationale: A named-pair exception a tier rule cannot express: lapidary-api may not depend on lapidary-cad because the open path lives there. A forbidden-pairs list beats an allow-list of api's permitted L2 deps — an allow-list must be edited every time api legitimately gains a dependency, and a list edited to permit ordinary work gets widened carelessly. Each entry carries its reason as the message, kept next to the rule rather than in a distant match arm.

nodes.label: SERVER_FEATURES
nodes.rationale: A build argument defaulting to empty so the api image links no kernel and the worker image does. Chosen over splitting the binary by role, which needs a role concept that does not exist until the worker leases jobs. The expansion must add no --features flag at all when empty — an empty --features "" is not the same thing.

nodes.label: Empty-State Copy Truthfulness
nodes.rationale: 'Drop a folder of STL or STEP files to begin' promised an interaction nothing implemented. Fixed now rather than deferred to Phase 1: the string ships in the UI today and tells users to do something that does nothing. The replacement must not promise an unimplemented affordance, must not read as an error (an empty library is a normal state), and stays in strings.ts.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 1 Handoff
nodes.rationale: Banner-superseded: written mid-plan after task 4 of 12, and everything it says about where execution stopped is now false. Kept rather than deleted because it is the only committed record of tasks 1-4's reasoning and review findings — the live ledger lives in the gitignored .superpowers/sdd/.

nodes.label: Tests That Claim a Mechanism
nodes.rationale: A test whose name claims a mechanism and whose body asserts an outcome that holds anyway. a_closed_cube_measures_its_bbox_and_volume passed with vertex quantisation entirely defeated, because the plan's cube fixture shares literal float values across facets in a way real STL never does. For any test naming a mechanism, ask what mutation would break the mechanism and confirm the test fails under it.

nodes.label: Migration Rebuild Gap
nodes.rationale: cargo does not rebuild the test binary when only a .sql migration changes, so sqlx::migrate!'s embedded migrations go stale and you get a green run against the old schema. Hit twice independently. A five-line build.rs emitting cargo:rerun-if-changed=migrations fixes it; harmless in CI, but it will bite the next slice's first migration.

nodes.label: Deliberate StoredBlob Duplication
nodes.rationale: StoredBlob in lapidary-storage and StoredBlobRow in lapidary-db are duplicated on purpose: both are L1 and check-layers forbids L1 to L1 dependencies, so the api layer converts. Recorded explicitly so a later reader does not 'fix' it.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 1 — Local Ingest to a Visible Grid
nodes.rationale: Twelve tasks turning a mesh file in a mounted directory into a card with a real rendered thumbnail. A read-only mounted directory is walked by a scan endpoint that mounts only in the worker role; new files are parsed, rasterized, written to a content-addressed blob store and recorded in one transaction.
nodes.norm_label: phase 1 slice 1 — local ingest to a visible grid

nodes.label: Hash-First Short-Circuit
nodes.rationale: BLAKE3 before anything else in ingest. A known hash short-circuits the whole pipeline, which is what makes re-dropping the same folder complete in seconds instead of re-parsing and re-rendering every file.

nodes.label: Role-Aware Router
nodes.rationale: router(state) becomes router(state, role), breaking both existing call sites on purpose: a route can no longer mount without declaring which role serves it. lapidary-server reads LAPIDARY_ROLE and selects the router; the scan endpoint mounts only under Role::Worker.

nodes.label: Blob CAS
nodes.rationale: Content-addressed blob store split into SourceStore and DerivativeStore so the open-path boundary is expressible in the type system — lapidary-api may not so much as name SourceStore. Content addressing is not authorization: knowing a blob hash never grants access.

nodes.label: MeshKernel
nodes.rationale: Wires parse_stl, measure and render_thumbnail behind the existing Kernel trait, and is the first consumer of RASTER_VERSION — which must be embedded in KernelVersion because derivative.kernel_version is the only thing distinguishing a regenerated thumbnail from a stale one.

nodes.label: CPU Thumbnail Rasterizer
nodes.rationale: Mesh to 512px WebP bytes, CPU only, with a downscale-and-retry fallback under a byte budget. image 0.25.10 encodes WebP with no C dependency and its whole tree is inside deny.toml's allow-list — checked before it was written into the plan, not after.

nodes.label: MeshMeasurements
nodes.rationale: With Provenance, the vocabulary both the kernel and the DB speak. Measurement must not lie: mesh-derived values are labelled approximate, and where the honest answer is no answer, write NULL rather than a plausible number.

nodes.label: Keyset-Paginated Grid Endpoint
nodes.rationale: GET /api/libraries/{id}/parts returns thumbnails inline as bytea so a page costs one query. sqlx 0.9 has no jiff feature, so the grid query selects microseconds and rebuilds through jiff::Timestamp::from_microsecond — caught by verifying rather than assuming, before the plan was written.

nodes.label: The Verification Bar
nodes.rationale: Exactly what ci.yml runs, and a task is not done until it passes: fmt, clippy -D warnings, check-layers, check-deploy, the test suite against a live PostgreSQL 18, and cargo deny. It grows over slices as gaps are found — check-strings, export-bindings, export-agents-md, check-commit-msg, and finally the web suite. Never pipe these through tail or grep when the exit code matters; a pipeline reports its last command's status.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 2 — Job Queue and Leased Worker
nodes.rationale: Turns the synchronous scan into durable per-file jobs drained by a leased worker, so killing the worker mid-scan loses only the files actually in flight. Fourteen tasks.
nodes.norm_label: phase 1 slice 2 — job queue and leased worker

nodes.label: PgJobs
nodes.rationale: Every statement the queue issues, plus the PgListener factory. All the queue's SQL lives here because no SQL goes outside lapidary-db — lapidary-jobs contains not one string of it.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED Leasing
nodes.rationale: Workers lease rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so concurrent workers never contend for the same job and losing the race for a file settles as a skip rather than a failure.

nodes.label: Reclamation Without a Reaper
nodes.rationale: Reclaiming expired leases is folded into the dequeue statement itself, so there is no reaper process to deploy, supervise, or forget to run. One fewer moving part in an air-gapped deployment.

nodes.label: LISTEN/NOTIFY over a Poll Floor
