nodes.rationale: LISTEN/NOTIFY wakes the loop early, but the 5-second polling floor is the actual correctness mechanism — a dropped notification costs latency, not work. A later handoff records that the listener test proved 'an idle loop notices cancellation' rather than 'the poll floor discovers work enqueued while the worker sleeps', which is what this design is about.

nodes.label: JobHandler
nodes.rationale: The seam that exists because of layering: lapidary-jobs is L2 and may not depend on lapidary-cad (L2) or lapidary-ingest (L3). lapidary-jobs owns delivery and policy and never learns what a mesh is; lapidary-ingest implements the trait with slice 1's per-file body.

nodes.label: next_state
nodes.rationale: A pure function from (result, attempts) to the next row state. Retry policy lives here and is tested here, without a database or a worker loop.

nodes.label: batch_id as a Column
nodes.rationale: One job row per file, grouped by a batch_id that is a column rather than an entity. batch_status counts rows by batch_id with no stored total, so the aggregate is computed rather than cached — which is what later lets a growing batch work at all.

nodes.label: Crash Resumption
nodes.rationale: The slice's whole claim — killing the worker mid-scan loses nothing but the files actually in flight — tested as stated end to end, not inferred from unit tests of its parts.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 2 Handoff
nodes.rationale: All 14 tasks landed. Exit run against 150 real STLs rather than the six repository fixtures, because the fixtures drain in about 70 ms — not long enough to kill a worker mid-scan with any reliability. SIGKILL at 52 done / 4 running / 94 pending came back as 150 ingested, 0 failed.

nodes.label: Reachable, Not Merely Up
nodes.rationale: Seven tests failed with PoolTimedOut while podman ps said 'Up 2 hours' and in-container pg_isready reported accepting connections: the rootless port forwarder had died while the container stayed healthy internally. docker ps and an in-container pg_isready answer the same wrong question. Use a host-side TCP connect — 'container up' and 'container reachable' are different claims and only the second is the one the tests depend on.

nodes.label: One Implementer per Worktree
nodes.rationale: Two tasks died mid-flight with their work intermingled and uncommitted in one tree. They were separated by inspection of which file belonged to which task, not by guessing, and committed separately so history stays honest. Note also that git commit commits the whole index, not just what one agent added.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 3 Handoff
nodes.rationale: Twelve tasks, twelve commits. Exit run showed 151 x 4 derivative rows, 15/15 rungs clean through Khronos gltf-validator, L0 86.1% smaller than L2 across the corpus, and throughput up rather than down. The honest reading of the throughput rise is machine variance: the ladder did not cost 3x, it cost nothing measurable. Not proved: nothing reads a rung yet, and the corpus is 150 dense organic scenery STLs, so 86% should not be quoted as universal.

nodes.label: Reap Keyed on This Job's Bytes
nodes.rationale: The plan put the derivative reap on the record error arm only, but link_existing writes rungs too. The larger problem is the other direction: a rung is usually bytes an earlier revision already stores, so reaping on any failed ingest deletes a part that ingested perfectly well. The reap is keyed on 'this job introduced these bytes', asked of PgBlobs::exists — the same authority the source blob asks.
nodes.norm_label: reap keyed on this job's bytes

nodes.label: check-strings EXEMPT List
nodes.rationale: Pinned by line number, so any edit above an exempt line shifts it and the gate goes stale. It went stale five times during one slice. Keying on a content fingerprint would end it.

nodes.label: Fixtures Too Coarse to Discriminate
nodes.rationale: Three mutations did not bite as written, all the same mistake. The 20-triangle bracket is coarser than L0's own grid, so its rungs are identical by design and no ladder mutation can change them; a collapsed cell is usually also touched by a surviving triangle, so it needed a deliberate fixture of one large triangle plus one tiny isolated one. In this repo, 'pick the standard fixture' is not a safe default for any test about cluster output.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 3 — The LOD Ladder
nodes.rationale: Every ingested mesh gets three glTF rungs alongside its thumbnail, stored by hash and served over an authorized blob route, so Phase 3's viewer has something to open. No new dependencies — not for clustering, not for glTF.

nodes.label: LOD Ladder
nodes.rationale: L2 at measure.rs's existing 1e-4 mm quantisation is lossless de-duplication; L1 and L0 at bbox/96 and bbox/32 are the lossy rungs. A mesh coarser than L0's own grid clusters to itself, and content addressing then makes its three identical rungs one blob with three references.

nodes.label: Vertex Clustering
nodes.rationale: One indexing function run at three grid sizes produces the whole ladder, rather than three algorithms or a clustering dependency. Collapsed cells are dropped.

nodes.label: write_glb
nodes.rationale: Hand-written uncompressed glTF 2.0 binary. DATA.md's meshopt choice stands but is not implemented here: its decoder is Phase 3's viewer and its Rust binding wraps C, which would put a C toolchain in the worker image. kernel_version carries glb-1 so Phase 3 can find these and re-encode.

nodes.label: Kernel Takes Bytes
nodes.rationale: The Kernel trait starts taking bytes rather than a path because the shipped code's refusal to re-read the file is right — the bytes are already in hand from hashing, and re-reading is both slower and a second chance for the file to change underneath.

nodes.label: KernelOutput
nodes.rationale: MeshOutput is deleted and KernelOutput becomes the one output type, with Entity added for analytic geometry. Its shape had been Phase 0a follow-up item 2, open since Phase 0a; Entity ships uninhabited, so no measurement snaps to analytic geometry yet.

nodes.label: GET /api/blob/{blake3}
nodes.rationale: Reachability is the authorization check: content addressing is not authorization, so the route verifies the hash is reachable from the caller's tenant rather than trusting knowledge of the hash. A malformed hash gets the same 404 as an unknown one, because a 400 would separate well-formed-but-absent from malformed — a smaller version of the oracle the reachability check exists to close.

nodes.label: derivative_storage_is_exclusive
nodes.rationale: A derivative is stored inline or by hash, never both and never neither. Both columns had been nullable and independent since migration 0002, so a row with neither was legal — and a row with neither is a derivative that cannot be served. derivative.blake3 also becomes a foreign key to blob. Verified against a migrated database rather than assumed, because a migration that fails on real data fails at deploy rather than in CI.

nodes.label: parse_obj
nodes.rationale: Shares stl.rs's finish gate rather than duplicating the validity checks, so both parsers reject the same malformed shapes for the same reasons. Its fixture is a real part with a plausible number, not cube.obj with three vertices.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 3b — 3MF Ingest
nodes.rationale: Split out of slice 3 so that adding the workspace's first ZIP and first XML dependency gets a review of its own rather than riding along with geometry work. Writes no SQL at all.

nodes.label: parse_3mf
nodes.rationale: Reads the OPC package with zip, follows _rels/.rels to the model part, and streams its XML with quick-xml, merging every build item's transformed mesh into the one Mesh the rest of the pipeline already handles. One file rather than four, because splitting .rels resolution from the mesh parse would put two halves of one decision in two files.

nodes.label: Caps
nodes.rationale: Zip-bomb defence: decompressed size, entry count, ratio and path traversal, applied as bytes arrive rather than after. Each breach must name which bound fired — sharing one error message across two bounds is how the absolute size cap went untested behind the ratio cap.

nodes.label: read_capped
nodes.rationale: Refuses as bytes arrive, not after. The mutation proving it must use a bounded source that counts bytes pulled: read_to_end on an infinite reader does not hang, it allocates until the OOM killer fires — it took the machine down twice at 10.9 GB and 13.2 GB on a 15 GB host.

nodes.label: Compression
nodes.rationale: SourceStore::put takes a compression policy so an already-compressed container like 3MF is stored as-is. Proven by measurement rather than assertion: the 3MF row saved 0.0% while the OBJ beside it saved 49.6% and the STLs 79.7-92.7%, which is what makes it a policy rather than compression having stopped working.

nodes.label: Build Transforms and Component Recursion
nodes.rationale: A multi-item build plate is one part with its triangles summed and its bbox spanning the placements. Both the transform/scale ordering and the composition order shipped correct and unpinned: a translation in a millimetre file has scale 1, a pure scale matrix commutes with a scalar, and identity 3x3 blocks make a transposed product give the same answer — so both orderings passed every test.

nodes.label: Dependency Audit as Its Own Slice
nodes.rationale: cargo-deny was not installed on the machine, and auditing the two new dependencies is the slice's whole premise — so task 1 installs it and runs it for real rather than deferring to CI. Two dependencies, both named in the spec, and no others: if a task feels like it needs a third, it is the wrong task.
nodes.norm_label: dependency audit as its own slice

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 3b Handoff
nodes.rationale: Ten tasks, seventeen commits. Closes ROADMAP.md's Phase 1 mesh-format line — STL, OBJ and 3MF all ingest to the same thumbnail and the same three rungs, and no migration was needed, which is the evidence slice 3's seam was cut in the right place.

nodes.label: Caps::max_triangles
nodes.rationale: MAX_DEPTH bounds recursion depth; nothing bounded breadth, and the work is branching^depth. A 604-byte package emitted 16,777,216 triangles at roughly a million times amplification — a sub-kilobyte file would kill a worker limited to 2 GiB, worse than refusing it because the process dies, the lease drops, and the retry feeds the same file back in. Checked as triangles accumulate. Refusing at the budget means doing the work up to it: 7.7 s at 278 MB peak RSS, recorded as a known ceiling.

nodes.label: quick-xml Security Floor
nodes.rationale: quick-xml 0.37 carried RUSTSEC-2026-0194 (quadratic-time parse) and RUSTSEC-2026-0195 (unbounded namespace-declaration allocation). Both sit in the one component that reads attacker-controlled XML, so they would have hollowed out the caps the slice exists to provide. Pinned at 0.41 and recorded in the spec as a security floor with the RUSTSEC ids.

nodes.label: Whole-Branch Adversarial Review
nodes.rationale: Every task passed its own review with spec compliance clean, and the whole-branch review then found a Critical. Per-task reviews could not see it: each was asked 'does this code match its brief?', and it did — the defect was in the plan. Only a reviewer looking at the whole path with permission to be adversarial had the standing to find it.

nodes.label: Tests That Could Not Fail
nodes.rationale: Five tests passed for the wrong reason, all authored in the plan rather than the implementations: std::io::repeat's specialised read_to_end made the naive implementation error too; unpinned transform and composition ordering; a zip-bomb fixture with no _rels/.rels that never reached the cap it was named for. Each fix was the same shape — assert the specific number or the specific message, never merely that an error occurred. A bare expect_err is how this keeps happening.

nodes.label: Per-Service Resource Ceilings
nodes.rationale: deploy.resources.limits added mid-slice at the owner's request: worker 2.0 cores and 2 GiB, and concurrency halved to 2. Throughput fell from 89.4 to 42.8 files/s while peak memory stayed at 2% of the ceiling, so the trade was CPU for fit — the stack now runs on a machine without gigabytes to spare, and raising LAPIDARY_WORKER_CONCURRENCY recovers throughput where there is room. Verified as actually applied via docker inspect, not merely declared.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — The Remaining Slices, Re-Cut
nodes.rationale: Slices 1-3b built ingest but not a system anyone can use: the web UI is a single read-only page and putting a file in means dropping it in a mounted folder and curling the worker, because the Caddyfile proxies only to api:8080. Carries a 2026-09-06 amendment that leaves the original table intact — it is the evidence for why the re-cut happened, and rewriting it would destroy the record.

nodes.label: Usable at Slice 5
nodes.rationale: The re-cut adds and drops nothing from ROADMAP.md's Phase 1 bullets; it moves only where the slice boundaries fall, so a usable storage-and-display system arrives at the end of slice 5 rather than at the end of the phase. part_image moves out of slice 4 because it is UI work and keeping it there made slice 4 two slices wearing one coat.

nodes.label: zstd Cold Tier Deferred
nodes.rationale: Measured on 143 MB of the real corpus: zstd -19 costs 38x the compression CPU of -3 for four percentage points. DATA.md's 6-10x estimate is for STEP, which is text; its own binary-STL estimate of ~2-2.5x is what the measurement confirms. Decompression is level-independent and effectively free, so no 'decompressing' indicator is needed either. The cold tier waits for Phase 2's STEP, where it may pay.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Exit Criterion
nodes.rationale: Drop a folder of 1,000 STLs, the grid is interactive immediately, all thumbnails land, re-dropping completes in seconds via the hash short-circuit, and the grid page loads under 80 ms warm. The 'all thumbnails land' clause is later reversed by on-demand rendering.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 4 Handoff
nodes.rationale: Ten tasks, twenty-five commits. Derivative bytes fell 92.5% on the same corpus slice 3 measured, and the L0 half matching slice 3's 7.3 MB to within its own rounding is the check that the two runs measure the same thing. Records thirty-one rulings, four briefed assertions that could not fail, and three cases where an implementer's own mutation found more than the briefed one.

nodes.label: Generated-File Freshness Is Not a Typecheck
nodes.rationale: tsc --noEmit was red for nine tasks and no gate noticed. The per-task bar ran eight Rust gates plus export-bindings, which regenerates and diffs the generated files — it proved BatchStatus.ts was current, which it was. Nothing in the bar compiled the TypeScript that consumes those bindings, and npm test passes regardless because vitest transpiles without typechecking. cargo deny and the web suite are permanently in the bar from here.
nodes.norm_label: generated-file freshness is not a typecheck

nodes.label: Cross-Tenant Scoping at the Query
nodes.rationale: Two findings, one a leak and one a write. An unscoped batch-status failure join leaked another library's part name; revision_source taking only a revision id let a derive job render onto another library's revision. Both raised by implementers who judged them out of scope and both overruled on placement for the same reason: a guard that lives away from the query it guards is the one that gets dropped.

nodes.label: CoreError::MalformedJobPayload
nodes.rationale: Its message told operators the row 'was not written by Lapidary'. But JobPayload::from_row exists precisely because an older Lapidary wrote rows a newer one must read, so version skew is the expected way to reach this error and the message pointed at the one cause that is not it. Fixed with a test that fails if the claim returns — nothing outside src/ pinned the wording, which is how it survived.

nodes.label: Re-Derivation Determinism
nodes.rationale: Two independent runs on separate volumes and separate databases wrote 7,501,328 bytes of L0 both times, and the on-demand L2 came out as the same BLAKE3 both times. Content addressing means a re-derivation is free of drift by construction — here it is observed rather than argued, which is what makes on-demand deriving safe.

nodes.label: Stale Progress on a Hidden Tab
nodes.rationale: react-query does not fire refetchInterval on a hidden document, so a user who starts a 10,000-part sweep and switches tabs returns to a progress line frozen at whatever the last poll saw. Nothing is lost and a reload shows the truth, but the page tells a stale story. index.tsx already reasons about the other half — not leaving a closed laptop asking about a completed scan forever — and this is the missing half.
nodes.norm_label: stale progress on a hidden tab

nodes.label: Briefed Assertions That Could Not Fail
nodes.rationale: Four assertions would have passed against the bug they named, all in briefs rather than implementations: a migration-survival test whose 'pre-existing' rows were inserted after the migration ran; a byte-identity mutation that changed a recorded column and never reached the bytes; a fixture too coarse to drift; and a toggle assertion that passes in both worlds because an unknown toggle also renders unchecked.
nodes.norm_label: briefed assertions that could not fail

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 4 Resume
nodes.rationale: Paused after task 7 at the owner's request. Instructs the successor to read the test count from cargo rather than trust a number written in any document, because the previous slice's plan asserted a baseline that moved four times.

nodes.label: upsert_derivative Guards
nodes.rationale: Refuse a hash-addressed thumbnail — the grid reads only thumb_bytes, so such a row shows 'no preview yet' for a part that has one, and revisions_missing excludes that revision so the sweep never heals it. Refuse an empty Inline — it reaches the grid as a broken img. Both guards go inside upsert_derivative, before the transaction, not at its call sites, so a refusal orphans no blob row.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 4 — Derive Less, and Track Use
nodes.rationale: Ingest stops producing three quarters of what it produces today, and the system starts recording when a blob was last touched. No new dependencies. Its own baseline line tells the reader to check cargo for the current test count rather than trusting the document — a stale baseline is how a task convinces itself it broke nothing.
nodes.norm_label: phase 1 slice 4 — derive less, and track use

nodes.label: Derive On Demand
nodes.rationale: Ingest asks for L0 only, plus a thumbnail when the library wants one; a derive job kind asks for exactly one thing against one revision, so L1 and L2 arrive when something wants them. Targets ~665 MB to ~48 MB of derivatives per 1,000 parts. Safe because content addressing makes re-derivation byte-identical, and because a part with no thumbnail still appears in the grid.

nodes.label: KernelParams.produce
nodes.rationale: A list of what this call must make, so the kernel builds what the caller asked for and nothing else. KernelOutput.tessellations becomes a Vec and cluster.rs's ladder() is deleted. The whole rung-filing behaviour rests on one test, recorded as concentration risk rather than a defect.

nodes.label: library.auto_thumbnail
nodes.rationale: A per-library setting, default on, added by migration 0005 alongside widening the outcome CHECK to accept 'rendered'. Migration 0005 removes no row. The UI toggle renders indeterminate and disabled before its GET resolves rather than showing a confident 'on' that flips.

nodes.label: JobPayload
nodes.rationale: A typed payload discriminated by the existing job.kind COLUMN rather than serde's tag attribute, so every pre-existing {"path": ...} row still deserialises. The old untyped path had a worse failure than a bad message: payload.get("path") succeeds on any ingest-shaped payload, so an unknown kind fell through to a file read, returned Transient, and the queue retried a job it could never run three times before failing.

nodes.label: blob.last_accessed_at
nodes.rationale: The column existed since migration 0002 and nothing wrote it, yet every storage feature after this depends on it. Written by the blob route only, never in the handler — a sweep touching blobs would mark everything warm and destroy the signal. Measured proof: exactly 2 of 301 rows carried a timestamp after the exit run, the two rungs actually fetched.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 5 Handoff
nodes.rationale: Exit criterion met: scan a folder from the browser, browse it, download a file and diff it against the one you started with, without a terminal. Explicitly refuses to compare 48 files/s against slice 4's 84.1 — different configurations. The comparable figure is the derivative total, which decomposes exactly into slice 4's L0 figure plus its separately-measured thumbnail bytes, a stronger cross-check because it is reproducible.

nodes.label: HEAD Warms a Blob
nodes.rationale: get(handler) routes HEAD, so the handler runs to completion and warms the blob while delivering nothing; blob.rs has the identical shape. Recorded rather than guarded because a guard would quietly answer a question slice 7 must answer openly. Escalation trigger written down: if a compression sweep ships first, a prefetcher or uptime check marks a library warm and the sweep skips exactly the blobs nobody downloads.

nodes.label: The Walk Is Retryable and Not Idempotent
nodes.rationale: Moving the walk into a job made it retryable where a request was not. Bounded 3x by max_attempts and duplicates settle as skipped so nothing ingests twice, but a first scan can report '150 added, 150 already here'. Recorded in scan.rs beside the reversal it cost.
nodes.norm_label: the walk is retryable and not idempotent

nodes.label: Derivative Ratio at Small Scale
nodes.rationale: Derivatives were 237.5% of sources on the six-part example folder and 18.1% on the 150-file corpus. Real data, but the label invites the wrong conclusion at small scale. Related known gaps: a blob shared across libraries is charged in full to each, and a blob reachable as both a file and a derivative counts in both totals.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 5 — Drive It From a Browser
nodes.rationale: Ten gates, not eight. Every task names a code change that makes its new test fail, runs it, captures the real output, and reverts byte-identically with md5sum before and after: a test whose mutation was never run is not a test. The plan is amended in place where execution proved a brief wrong, with the stale text called out rather than silently replaced.
nodes.norm_label: phase 1 slice 5 — drive it from a browser

nodes.label: SourceReader
nodes.rationale: A read-only handle with no WorkerRole, no put and no remove. It is not SourceStore because reading stored bytes for a user who asked for those exact bytes is not the open path, and the write surface is the half WorkerRole is worth spending on. Its decode flag is zstd_level != 0, corrected from > 0 — zstd spells --fast=N levels negative and a negative level still produces a frame, so > 0 would hand a compressed frame to a user as their file.

nodes.label: GET /api/revisions/{id}/download
nodes.rationale: variant=original returns byte-identical ingested bytes, making 'downloads are never silently converted' testable for the first time. Order of operations matters: resolve, 404, validate variant, 500 on an unrecorded zstd_level naming the blob, read, re-hash and 500 on mismatch, touch_blob, respond. The two 500 branches stay separate because their messages are — one says an operator has a blob row no ingest path wrote, the other says the bytes on disk are not the bytes we recorded.

nodes.label: check_open_path_boundary
nodes.rationale: Greps for literal type names in lapidary-api: SourceStore is forbidden outright, and SourceReader may appear only in a file whose path ends download.rs. A boundary expressed as a per-file allowance rather than a blanket ban, so the one route that legitimately reads source bytes is named and every other one still fails the gate.

nodes.label: RFC 5987 Content-Disposition
nodes.rationale: Both an ASCII fallback and filename*=UTF-8'' encoding, with the filename synthesized and sanitized for path separators, control characters and quotes. The fixture uses a real Turkish part name rather than an ASCII one with a comment about Turkish. The encoder's allowlist is load-bearing: adding %, ' and * left the suite green while reintroducing a path traversal through RFC 8187 client decoding.

nodes.label: JobPayload::ScanDirectory
nodes.rationale: A deliberate reversal of scan.rs's own module doc, recorded where that reasoning is written and not only in the plan. The original brief could not have been built: enqueue_scan takes a path list produced by walking /ingest, which the api container does not mount. What makes the reversal honest rather than convenient is that the module doc's objection — a failure goes unseen — is answered by rendering the failure reasons, which batch_status already returned and nothing displayed. Alternatives rejected: a Caddy route to worker:8081 spans the browser's API surface across two backends with no gate watching the pattern; mounting /ingest on the api puts the ingest directory on the container whose whole point is reading metadata and derivatives.

nodes.label: enqueue_into
nodes.rationale: enqueue mints a fresh BatchId every call, so a scan job enqueuing its files into a new batch would let the UI poll the scan's own batch, see 1 of 1 complete, and report a finished scan while 150 files are still ingesting. The scan job puts its children in its own batch instead, which works because batch_status computes the aggregate rather than caching a stored total.

nodes.label: Storage Visibility
nodes.rationale: PartSummary grows revision, source_hash, source_bytes, stored_bytes and compressed via one more LATERAL — no migration, every column already on blob. The verifying SELECT is deliberately not the obvious one: sum over the distinct blobs a library's file rows reference, because summing the file rows double-counts a deduplicated library, and add sum(octet_length(thumb_bytes)) because every thumbnail is inline and has no blob row.

nodes.label: Storage Layout, Folder Tree and Moves
nodes.rationale: Turns the blob store into a browsable storage folder holding one directory per model — its source file, its metadata.json and its images — with PostgreSQL indexing the paths, a category tree the user can reorganise, and an audit log of where each model has been.
nodes.norm_label: storage layout, folder tree and moves

nodes.label: Path-Addressed Source Storage
nodes.rationale: Source files move from blobs/ab/cd/<hash> to libraries/<lib>/<category>/<model>/<file> so the store is browsable outside the app. Derivatives stay content-addressed under cache/, which keeps /api/blob/{hash}'s immutable caching and makes 'eviction is not data loss' self-evident. part.source_path stays the immutable ingest identity key; folder_id carries mutable location and file.storage_path carries the bytes' real path.

nodes.label: ModelManifest
nodes.rationale: The metadata.json shape and its schema version — what makes the store self-describing, so a model directory read without the database still says what it is.

nodes.label: PgFolders
nodes.rationale: Get-or-create, tree, cycle check, subtree delete and moves. Fixtures use real category paths like Terrain/Rocks/Cliffs, never 'Folder 1'.

nodes.label: part_move
nodes.rationale: An audit log of where each model has been, so a move is recoverable history rather than a silent overwrite of a location field.

nodes.label: JobPayload::MigrateStorage
nodes.rationale: Existing stores convert through a resumable job, not through the SQL migration. Moving every source file inside a migration would make a deploy an unbounded, uninterruptible filesystem operation with no progress and no way to resume.

nodes.label: slugify
nodes.rationale: With disambiguate and reject_escaping_path, filesystem-safe names in lapidary-core so the ingest handler's local path guard is deleted rather than duplicated — one guard all callers route through.

nodes.label: SourceRelocator
nodes.rationale: A third named type with exactly one allowed module in lapidary-api, following the SourceReader precedent: the boundary is a per-file allowance enforced by check-deploy rather than trust.

nodes.label: Dual-Layout Reads
nodes.rationale: Reads tolerate both layouts — download reads from storage_path and falls back to the CAS path — so the resumable migration can be half-finished without any part becoming unreadable.

nodes.label: Phase 0a — Greenfield Foundation
nodes.rationale: A fresh start rather than a staged migration from the Node prototype: the prototype survives on main and in history as a reference implementation, so nothing is lost by deleting it, and there is no half-migrated state to maintain.

nodes.label: L0-L3 Crate Layering Rule
nodes.rationale: Layering is enforced by an xtask over cargo metadata rather than cargo-deny, because deny's [bans] targets external crates and cannot express intra-workspace layering; an xtask is unit-testable against a synthetic graph and behaves identically locally and in CI. Superseded in part on 2026-09-02: lapidary-enterprise moved to its own Enterprise tier above L3.

nodes.label: cargo xtask check-layers
nodes.rationale: Its unit tests assert the rule catches an injected violation, not merely that today's graph passes.

nodes.label: lapidary-core (L0)
nodes.rationale: Carries genuine domain surface from day one so the ts-rs pipeline is real and the layering check has actual edges to police.

nodes.label: lapidary-db (L1)
nodes.rationale: The only crate permitted to depend on sqlx; ALL SQL lives here, enforced by deny.toml.

nodes.label: lapidary-api (L3)
nodes.rationale: A library that builds and returns a Router. Never a binary, never forked per distribution.

nodes.label: Kernel trait
nodes.rationale: The trait's shape is what is stable; KernelOutput's fields explicitly are not.

nodes.label: MockKernel
nodes.rationale: The boring option for 0a: subprocess spawn, timeout and crash handling land in 0b with the real sidecar rather than being written twice.

nodes.label: Approximate<T>
nodes.rationale: Makes 'mesh-derived, label it approximate' unavoidable at the type level rather than a UI convention.

nodes.label: LibraryMode (Hobby | Controlled)
nodes.rationale: Governance is opt-in per library, so the mode is a domain type from the start.

nodes.label: PartSummary
nodes.rationale: One `approximate: bool` is correct for a grid card, which wants one badge; the detail view legitimately differs in granularity.

nodes.label: ts-rs Binding Export Pipeline
nodes.rationale: web/src/bindings/ is committed, not gitignored, so CI can compare regenerated output against it and catch staleness; routeTree.gen.ts is committed for the same reason, because tsc runs before Vite on a clean clone.

nodes.label: web / api / worker / db Compose Topology
nodes.rationale: Four services, no Redis and no broker; cache is Postgres. Compose Spec syntax working under both podman compose and docker compose, with --env-file passed explicitly because the two runtimes disagree about auto-loading.
nodes.norm_label: web / api / worker / db compose topology

nodes.label: AGPL-3.0-only Single Workspace Licence
nodes.rationale: lapidary-enterprise stays AGPL; the Ed25519 licence file is a contractual and support boundary, not technical DRM. Keeps DCO, avoids a CLA.

nodes.label: Deletion of the Node Prototype
nodes.rationale: Accepted cost: no runnable application on the branch until Phase 1, so there is no live reference to diff behaviour against. Domain knowledge in server/src/services/ is recorded crate-by-crate before deletion.

nodes.label: Vite + React + TanStack SPA
nodes.rationale: Next.js would put a Node runtime in the production container; the later Tauri app bundles only our own binaries and cannot ship a Next server. SSR buys nothing for an authenticated tool that opens on a virtualized grid.

nodes.label: sqlx::migrate! Embedded Migrator
nodes.rationale: Migrations are embedded at compile time and applied at startup, so an image carries its own schema and an air-gapped operator needs no migration tooling on the host.

nodes.label: Pin Everything
nodes.rationale: Exact versions with no carets, container digests, Cargo.lock committed, GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs — so an air-gapped build reproduces.

nodes.label: Slice 1 — Local Ingest to a Visible Grid
nodes.rationale: Phase 1's five subsystems are sequenced as a vertical slice rather than in dependency order, because dependency order leaves nothing visible until the third slice. The cost is that ingest is written synchronously here and moved behind the queue in slice 2 — a trigger change, not a rewrite.
nodes.norm_label: slice 1 — local ingest to a visible grid

nodes.label: Hash-First Short-Circuit
nodes.rationale: BLAKE3 before anything else; a known hash skips parse, raster and write entirely. Scoped on library + part name + hash, not the hash alone: keying it on content alone let a content address decide a per-library write, and scanning six real STLs into an empty library reported six skips with the library still empty.

nodes.label: Blob CAS (BLAKE3, two-level hex sharding, ref_count)
nodes.norm_label: blob cas (blake3, two-level hex sharding, ref_count)

nodes.label: CPU-Rasterized 512px WebP Thumbnail
nodes.rationale: A GPU renderer makes output driver- and version-dependent, so byte-identical regeneration stops holding and golden-image tests become perceptual-diff tests with a tolerance. A Vulkan stack is also a large dependency and a driver-bug class that is miserable in air-gapped installs. Accepted cost: flat/matcap shading, adequate for triage.

nodes.label: Read-Only /ingest Mount
nodes.rationale: The scan route takes no path argument, so no caller-supplied path ever reaches the filesystem and traversal is structurally impossible rather than defended against. Read-only means an ingest bug cannot damage the user's library.

nodes.label: Per-Measurement Provenance Columns
nodes.rationale: volume_source and bbox_source sit beside the values they describe, because in Phase 2 a STEP revision has an analytic volume and a tessellated triangle count on the same row, and any single row-level flag must lie about one of them. triangle_count deliberately has no _source column: it cannot be analytic.

nodes.label: LAPIDARY_ROLE Route Split
nodes.rationale: Forced, not chosen: ingest must not run in the api process, whose image deliberately does not link lapidary-cad. Both containers run one binary with one router, so a role is the smallest thing that keeps the ingest path out of the open-path binary.

nodes.label: SourceStore
nodes.rationale: Obtainable only in the worker role. A dependency-graph rule cannot express the distinction, because depending on lapidary-storage is legitimate for derivatives; the distinction is which bytes, so it must be an API-level boundary.

nodes.label: DerivativeStore
nodes.rationale: Held by both roles: the api legitimately reads derivatives.

nodes.label: lapidary-ingest (L3)
nodes.rationale: The scan route does not live in lapidary-api: a handler there needing MeshKernel would force lapidary-api -> lapidary-cad and put the CAD kernel back in the api image. A separate L3 crate makes the boundary a dependency edge rather than a runtime if.

nodes.label: MeshKernel
nodes.rationale: STL parsing and rasterization are geometry, so they sit behind the kernel boundary — ingest invokes the kernel, opening a part never does.

nodes.label: STORED tsvector Search Column
nodes.rationale: Uses the simple configuration, not english or turkish: Phase 2 owns the real search design and part numbers must not be stemmed, so simple is the choice that does not pretend to have decided. The column exists now only because adding a generated column later is a table rewrite, and because PG 18's virtual default is easy to forget.

nodes.label: Migration-Seeded Default Library
nodes.rationale: The scan route needs an id and nothing in the slice creates a library. A fixed uuid in a migration is the seam to watch: whichever slice adds a second library must replace the seed, not build beside it.

nodes.label: Orphan Blob Reap Ordering
nodes.rationale: The blob is written before the transaction and a failed transaction reaps it — the prototype leaked an orphan on exactly this path. The reap runs only on the branch that wrote bytes; reaping a blob another library's part references would be silent data loss, so the two branches are separate calls rather than one call with a flag.

nodes.label: PgBlobs::library_holds
nodes.rationale: Deliberately does not filter deleted_at, so a re-scan reports a soft-deleted part as skipped rather than resurrecting it.

nodes.label: A Scan Is Not Transactional Across Files
nodes.rationale: One malformed STL must not abort the walk. Failures are collected as {file, reason} and returned with a 200 summary, because a partial success is the accurate description. The prototype counted skips with no reasons at all, which is why a failed import there was undiagnosable.
nodes.norm_label: a scan is not transactional across files

nodes.label: Volume Is NULL When the Mesh Is Not Watertight
nodes.rationale: Signed-volume integration over an open mesh returns a number that means nothing. 'Measurement must not lie' applied to the case where the honest answer is no answer.
nodes.norm_label: volume is null when the mesh is not watertight

nodes.label: Slice 2 — The Job Queue, and Ingest That Survives a Crash
nodes.rationale: Three defects in synchronous ingest drive the slice: the request is the unit of durability, the failure list lives only in a response body, and one scan is served by exactly one process — and a metered worker fleet that cannot split a folder is not a fleet.
nodes.norm_label: slice 2 — the job queue, and ingest that survives a crash

nodes.label: job table
nodes.rationale: batch_id is a grouping column with a partial dequeue index; job_done_has_outcome is an equivalence while job_failed_has_reason is only an implication, because a retrying job legitimately holds a last error while pending.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED Lease Dequeue
nodes.norm_label: for update skip locked lease dequeue

nodes.label: Lease Reclamation Folded Into the Dequeue
nodes.rationale: No sweeper process exists, so no sweeper process can be the thing that died. attempts increments on reclamation exactly as on retry, so the poison-pill case is capped by the same counter; the cap check lives in the loop rather than the SQL, because excluding exhausted rows in the WHERE clause would leave them running with an expired lease forever.
nodes.norm_label: lease reclamation folded into the dequeue

nodes.label: LISTEN/NOTIFY as an Optimization Over a Polling Floor
nodes.rationale: NOTIFY fires into the void when nothing is listening, so a worker that starts after an enqueue would never learn about that work if notification were the only path. The polling floor is the correctness mechanism; a test disables the listener entirely so the property cannot decay into 'notify happens to be what works'.
nodes.norm_label: listen/notify as an optimization over a polling floor

nodes.label: JobHandler trait
nodes.rationale: The layering rule forbids exactly the edge a naive worker loop would need, which produces the better design: lapidary-jobs owns delivery and policy and knows nothing about meshes; lapidary-ingest owns one file's work and knows nothing about leases.

nodes.label: HandlerError (Permanent | Transient)
nodes.rationale: When in doubt the classification is Transient: a retried permanent failure costs one wasted parse, while a non-retried transient failure costs the user a file.

nodes.label: A Parse Failure Is Terminal on the First Attempt
nodes.rationale: The bytes are content-addressed and immutable, so parsing the same blob again is guaranteed to produce the same error. The generic 'retry everything N times' default is wrong here for a reason specific to this system rather than a matter of taste.
nodes.norm_label: a parse failure is terminal on the first attempt

nodes.label: part_name_unique_per_library Constraint
nodes.rationale: Lease expiry means two workers can genuinely run the same job concurrently, and no amount of checking harder fixes it because the check is not atomic with the insert. The loser's unique violation maps to Outcome::Skipped, making at-least-once delivery effectively-once at the only place that can enforce it. Its key must agree with library_holds's filter.

nodes.label: BatchStatus
nodes.rationale: failed is capped at 100 and ordered by (created_at, id); the id tiebreaker is load-bearing because a whole batch is inserted in one transaction and Postgres's now() is constant per transaction, so ordering by created_at alone discriminates nothing.

nodes.label: batch_id Is a Grouping Column, Not a Row
nodes.rationale: There is no batch entity to keep consistent, so nothing can be stale because nothing is denormalized. The one cost is that a batch that enqueued nothing has no status resource and 404s.
nodes.norm_label: batch_id is a grouping column, not a row

nodes.label: Library-Scoped Batch Status Route
nodes.rationale: A batch id is a uuid the caller might hold from any source, and content addressing is not authorization. Scoping the route makes the ownership check structural rather than a step someone can forget to write.

nodes.label: Graceful Shutdown Releases Leases
nodes.rationale: In-flight jobs go back to pending with run_after = now(), so a planned restart resumes instantly instead of waiting out a 60-second lease. A crash does not get this, which is what lease expiry is for; only one of the two paths can run cleanup code.

nodes.label: The Worker Loop
nodes.rationale: The concurrency permit is acquired before the dequeue, never after: leasing a job we have no capacity to start would burn lease time in a queue, and a lease that expires while the job waits is indistinguishable from a crashed worker.

nodes.label: Lease Heartbeats Deferred
nodes.rationale: A 200 ms mesh ingest against a 60-second lease would renew a lease with 59.8 seconds left — ceremony that still has to be tested and can still be wrong. renew_lease lands when a job can realistically outlive its lease, which is STEP ingest through the OCCT sidecar.

nodes.label: Slice 3 — The LOD Ladder, OBJ, and One Kernel Output
nodes.rationale: Closes three places the codebase lied about itself: KernelOutput and MeshOutput were two unreconciled types, DerivativeStore had never run, and GET /api/blob/{blake3} did not exist.
nodes.norm_label: slice 3 — the lod ladder, obj, and one kernel output

nodes.label: Vertex-Clustering LOD Ladder (L0/L1/L2)
nodes.rationale: The whole ladder falls out of measure.rs's existing vertex-quantisation function at three grid sizes. Clustering does not need indexed input — it produces it — so Mesh stays an unindexed triangle soup and no re-parse or adjacency structure is needed. Grids are a fraction of the bounding box, not absolute, so a 5 mm screw and a 2 m gantry get comparable triangle counts.

nodes.label: Hand-Written glTF 2.0 Binary Writer
nodes.rationale: meshopt's Rust binding wraps C, which would put a C toolchain in the worker image and break the offline container build. Derivatives are designed to be thrown away, so writing plain GLB now and re-encoding in Phase 3 costs one regeneration pass over explicitly disposable data.

nodes.label: Kernel::process Takes Bytes, Not a Path
nodes.rationale: Ingest has already read and hashed the file, and reading it twice would be a second chance to read something different. Hashing before parsing is the ordering the whole pipeline rests on, so a kernel that re-opens the path can disagree with the hash already committed. The trait signature was the defect, not the code.
nodes.norm_label: kernel::process takes bytes, not a path

nodes.label: KernelOutput (reconciled)
nodes.rationale: entities stays Vec<Entity> rather than Vec<String> so Phase 3's measurement can snap to axes and radii instead of parsing 'CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE:22.000'. Its emptiness for mesh input is load-bearing: it is what stops tessellated numbers being presented as exact.

nodes.label: GET /api/blob/{blake3}
nodes.rationale: On the open path: it reads a derivative, never a source file, and never the kernel. Immutable caching is possible only because the URL contains the hash of what it returns.

nodes.label: Blob Reachability Check
nodes.rationale: Content addressing is not authorization — hashes leak into manifests, logs, bundles and support tickets, so knowing one must never be a capability. An unreferenced hash is a 404 whether or not the bytes are on disk. Written now while it is one join, rather than retrofitted in Phase 8 as a security fix.

nodes.label: Migration 0004 — Derivative Storage Discriminator
nodes.rationale: A derivative is stored inline or by hash, never both and never neither; and derivative.blake3 becomes a foreign key to blob, which is what makes ref_count cover derivatives and makes three identical rungs cost one blob instead of three.

nodes.label: kernel_version Names the Parser
nodes.rationale: derivative.kernel_version must change when output bytes could change, or a regenerated thumbnail is indistinguishable from a stale one. Once OBJ is ingested, a version reading stl-1 for an OBJ-derived thumbnail is exactly that lie, so the version names parser, tessellation writer and rasterizer independently.

nodes.label: Triangle-Budget Retry (halve the grid)
nodes.rationale: Follows raster.rs's existing thumbnail retry pattern. DATA.md's ~5k and ~50k are approximate and the retry keeps them approximately true across a corpus where a fixed grid would not; the grid actually used is recorded in params_json so the derivative says how it was made.

nodes.label: Format Dispatch on Extension, Not Byte Sniffing
nodes.rationale: OBJ is plain text with no magic number, so a sniffing implementation reduces to guessing from the first non-comment line. The extension is what the walk filtered on, so it is what the parser is told; a file whose extension lies becomes a per-file Permanent failure.
nodes.norm_label: format dispatch on extension, not byte sniffing

nodes.label: A Small Mesh Still Gets Three Rungs
nodes.rationale: The alternative puts a conditional into every consumer to save a few kilobytes on the smallest parts. Content addressing makes the waste nearly free: three identical .glb files are one blob with ref_count 3 — the rows differ, the bytes do not.
nodes.norm_label: a small mesh still gets three rungs

nodes.label: Slice 3b — 3MF Ingest
nodes.rationale: Split out of slice 3 because two formats with opposite risk profiles under one heading is what makes a slice overrun: an OBJ bug produces a wrong mesh, a 3MF bug is a denial of service. They deserve separate reviews.

nodes.label: Caps — Decompressed Size, Entries, Ratio, Triangles
nodes.rationale: Compiled in and not configurable: a security control with an environment override is one an operator can switch off by accident. Injectable in tests so the hostile fixture is a few hundred bytes rather than a multi-gigabyte file. Breach is checked as bytes arrive through Read::take — inflating an entry and then measuring it is the bomb working as designed.
nodes.norm_label: caps — decompressed size, entries, ratio, triangles

nodes.label: 3MF Unit Conversion to Millimetres
nodes.rationale: The first ingest path where the source states a unit. An absent unit defaults to millimetre per the 3MF core spec; an unrecognised one is refused rather than defaulted, because guessing millimetres for a file that said inch scales the part by 25.4 and produces measurements that are wrong, plausible and silent.

nodes.label: Component Recursion Depth Cap
nodes.rationale: An object may reference other objects in a cycle, which is an infinite loop on input we do not control. A depth cap ends it and costs one counter.

nodes.label: The Model Part Is Found Through the Relationships
nodes.rationale: Reading 3D/3dmodel.model directly would work for almost every file. Following _rels/.rels costs one small XML parse and lets a legal 3MF whose model lives elsewhere ingest, leaving only a genuinely malformed package as the failure.
nodes.norm_label: the model part is found through the relationships

nodes.label: Compression::{Zstd, AsIs} Source Policy
nodes.rationale: 3MF is already a deflate ZIP, so re-compressing it with zstd spends CPU on every ingest to make the file very slightly larger. The table lives in one place with its reasoning beside it, rather than as a boolean at a call site where the next reader cannot tell what true meant.

nodes.label: CadError::ArchiveRefused
nodes.rationale: A bomb may be perfectly well-formed, so 'Re-export it' is wrong advice for a file refused on size; an operator needs to know a limit fired rather than a parser failed.

nodes.label: zip + quick-xml Dependency Review
nodes.rationale: The hand-rolled parsers in this crate are geometry parsers, where a bug is a wrong mesh; a hand-rolled archive reader's bugs are vulnerabilities. Both crates are pure Rust so no C toolchain enters the worker image and cargo vendor still builds offline. quick-xml is pinned at 0.41 as a security floor: 0.37 carries RUSTSEC-2026-0194 and -0195, exactly the threats the caps exist to stop.

nodes.label: RAR Is a Licence Dead End
nodes.rationale: The corpus is distributed as .rar and the only complete decoder is the unrar C library, whose licence is not OSI-approved and collides with AGPL-3.0-only, cargo-deny's allow-list and cargo vendor. The archive slice must decide explicitly rather than discovering it.
nodes.norm_label: rar is a licence dead end

nodes.label: Post-Decompression Geometry Amplification
nodes.rationale: The three archive caps bound what comes out of the ZIP and say nothing about what the model then generates: components branching gives geometry as branching^depth, and a 604-byte package emitted 16.7M triangles at ~10^6x amplification. Caps::max_triangles closes it, checked as triangles accumulate rather than after.

nodes.label: Slice 4 — Derive Less, and Let a Part Carry a Real Picture
nodes.rationale: Slice 3's exit run measured that L2 is a lossless re-encode of a source blob that is never deleted, so half of all derivative storage duplicated data the system keeps anyway. Derivative storage drops roughly 93%.
nodes.norm_label: slice 4 — derive less, and let a part carry a real picture

nodes.label: Ingest Stores L0 Only
nodes.rationale: Reverses DATA.md 2.1, which weighed first-open latency against nothing and was written before 'must run on a modest workstation' was a stated constraint. The principle it leans on is the same document's own: a derivative that may be evicted and regenerated is a derivative that need not exist yet. The warning is accepted as the price — L0 is already there, so the viewer paints immediately and refines.

nodes.label: library.auto_thumbnail
nodes.rationale: Default on, because the alternative fails the product: 1,000 STLs into a library with rendering off is 1,000 blank cards, and a visual index whose cards are blank is not one. Off is for a large or low-powered library.

nodes.label: derive Job Kind
nodes.rationale: One kind, not two. 'Render a thumbnail' and 'build L2' are the same procedure differing only in the last step, and the (revision_id, kind) upsert means the discriminator already is the derivative kind.

nodes.label: JobPayload — the Column Is the Discriminator
nodes.rationale: An internally-tagged #[serde(tag = "kind")] enum was specified and is wrong: every job row written so far holds a bare {"path": ...} with no kind key, so on upgrade every pending job would become undeserialisable and the queue would stop draining. The column stays the discriminator and the payload carries only the variant's fields, so old and new rows are indistinguishable and no migration is needed.
nodes.norm_label: jobpayload — the column is the discriminator

nodes.label: The Payload Names a Revision, Not a Part
nodes.rationale: A part-scoped payload would make the handler resolve 'the latest revision' independently of the grid's LATERAL, and two resolutions that must agree is a bug waiting for a second revision: render revision B, show revision A's row.
nodes.norm_label: the payload names a revision, not a part

nodes.label: A User Image Is Bounded Inline WebP, Not a Blob
nodes.rationale: A photograph is never re-derivable, which puts it in the Source class — but SourceStore needs WorkerRole and the worker is unreachable from the browser, while DerivativeStore is evicted freely, so user data there plants a data-loss bug inside the future 'clear render cache' action. The original upload is not retained, only the bounded re-encode; refusing to store something at the boundary and saying so is not implicit deletion.
nodes.norm_label: a user image is bounded inline webp, not a blob

nodes.label: blob.last_accessed_at
nodes.rationale: Every age-based storage feature depends on it, and a column that has never been populated is worth nothing at the moment you first want it.

nodes.label: The Cold Compression Tier Is Deliberately Not Built
nodes.rationale: Measured on 143 MB of real STL: zstd -19 costs 38x the compression CPU of -3 for four percentage points, because nearly all of the available win is already taken at ingest. The same measurement settles a UX question — decompression is level-independent and effectively free, so no 'decompressing...' affordance is needed.
nodes.norm_label: the cold compression tier is deliberately not built

nodes.label: Every Trigger Route Is on Role::Api
nodes.rationale: Necessity, not preference: Caddy proxies /api/* to api:8080 only, so a route mounted under Role::Worker is unreachable from the UI. Enqueueing is a database write, so a trigger route needs neither the kernel nor ingest_dir; the rendering still happens in the worker.
nodes.norm_label: every trigger route is on role::api

nodes.label: Slice 5 — Drive It From a Browser
nodes.rationale: The plan's framing was wrong: this was never an access problem. The api already mounts the blob volume read-write, SourceStore and DerivativeStore read the same file, and WorkerRole is a naming and ownership gate enforced by a grep.
nodes.norm_label: slice 5 — drive it from a browser

nodes.label: SourceReader
nodes.rationale: Read-only: open(root) with no proof, get, no put, no remove. Relaxing the SourceStore gate instead would hand the api put and remove on source bytes to buy a read, and the write surface is the half of that type worth gating.

nodes.label: GET /api/revisions/{id}/download?variant=original
nodes.rationale: No library segment, matching DATA.md: resolving the library from the revision and then checking it against itself is a no-op that reads like a check, which is worse than no check. Filters part.deleted_at IS NULL so a held URL does not outlive a delete.

nodes.label: Download Is Not Open
nodes.rationale: The open-path rule is about opening — the grid, the viewer, the detail card, the path whose budget is 80 ms and whose failure mode is parsing STEP to draw a thumbnail. Download is a distinct, deliberately-named path that streams stored bytes to a user who asked for those exact bytes and parses nothing; the byte-identity product rule cannot be satisfied without it.

nodes.label: RFC 5987 Content-Disposition Filename
nodes.rationale: Both halves — an ASCII filename= fallback and filename*=UTF-8'' — because Turkish part names carry g-breve, s-cedilla and dotless i and a naive filename= mangles the download. The fixture carries a Turkish name rather than an ASCII one with a comment about Turkish.

nodes.label: Re-Hash the Bytes Before Serving Them
nodes.rationale: BLAKE3 at ~1 GB/s is free next to the transfer that follows, and it makes the product claim actually true rather than asserted. It also closes the hole ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING leaves: a crash between write_blob's rename and the commit can leave a file with no row, and a later ingest under a different format writes a row whose level does not match those bytes.
nodes.norm_label: re-hash the bytes before serving them

nodes.label: LibraryStorage Totals Panel
nodes.rationale: A blob-only sum reports 0 B of derivatives for a library where every part has a preview, because thumbnails live inline in derivative.thumb_bytes with no blob row; and summing over file rows rather than distinct blobs double-counts a deduplicated library. The ratio is computed server-side so two consumers cannot report the same library upside down.

nodes.label: HEAD Warms last_accessed_at
nodes.rationale: axum's get(handler) also routes HEAD and the handler runs to completion before the body is discarded, so a HEAD moves the timestamp while handing nobody any bytes. Both blob.rs and download.rs have the identical shape, so it is a property of both routes rather than a bug in one, and patching a single handler would be the wrong shape of fix.

nodes.label: check_open_path_boundary Grep Gate
nodes.rationale: A green run proves 'nothing named SourceStore directly', not 'no source bytes are reachable'. It gains one assertion per read handle — SourceReader only in download.rs — because a handle in one named route is a decision and the same handle in six files is the mistake arrived at by copy-paste.

nodes.label: blob.zstd_level Decides Decompression
nodes.rationale: Not Compression::for_source_format, which is ingest-time policy that slice 7 is about to change; a reader that re-derives policy would start returning zstd frames the day the policy moves. A NULL level on a source blob is not 'raw' — it is 'nobody recorded how these bytes were stored' — and the route answers 500 naming the blob rather than falling through to a hash mismatch that explains nothing.

nodes.label: Forward Constraint — Row First, Then Bytes
nodes.rationale: In-place recompression rewrites bytes and updates zstd_level with no transaction spanning both. Row-first shows level 3 over raw bytes, which fails loudly; bytes-first shows level 0 over a zstd frame and would return the frame as if it were the file. Slice 7 writes the row first, or sniffs frame magic; picking neither is not an option.
nodes.norm_label: forward constraint — row first, then bytes

nodes.label: Storage Layout and Folders — A Store the User Can Open
nodes.rationale: Reverses two written decisions on the owner's explicit instruction: the blob store becomes a user-owned host directory rather than a named volume, and source files become path-addressed rather than content-addressed.
nodes.norm_label: storage layout and folders — a store the user can open

nodes.label: Path-Addressed, Browsable Store
nodes.rationale: The cost, stated plainly: identical bytes in two models are two copies on disk, and it is not recoverable by cleverness — a store cannot both be one file per model and one file per distinct content. What survives is 'hash first, always': library_holds keys on (library_id, source_path, blake3), so hashing still happens first and a re-scan still settles as Skipped. Only the filename the bytes are written under changes.

nodes.label: Model Directory Naming and Slug Rules
nodes.rationale: Slugify the part name and append the first six hex characters of the blake3 on collision. Directory names are cosmetic, not identity — nothing parses them — which lets the naming optimise for a human reading a file manager. Unicode is preserved, Windows-reserved characters are replaced, trailing dots and spaces are trimmed, and device names get a _ suffix, because a model legitimately called AUX is not hypothetical in a parts library.
nodes.norm_label: model directory naming and slug rules

nodes.label: metadata.json — A Self-Describing Store
nodes.rationale: Carries enough to rebuild the rows, so deleting the database still leaves the store describing itself; there is no separate manifest directory because a manifest not beside the thing it describes goes stale. It is machine-owned and the user may delete it, so it is not defended but degraded around: a directory with no readable metadata.json is an orphan that re-adoption skips and reports.

nodes.label: file.storage_path
nodes.rationale: Stays nullable: null means the bytes are still at the old content-addressed path, which is a live state for as long as migrate_storage takes to drain — hours on a real corpus, so a supported state rather than an edge case.

nodes.label: part.source_path Never Changes
nodes.rationale: Three columns, three jobs: source_path is where the file was when we first saw it, folder_id is where the user has since put it, storage_path is where the bytes actually sit. Mutating source_path on a move means a re-scan of the original directory stops recognising the file, ingests it a second time and reports success — the silent duplication 6a exists to refuse.

nodes.label: Rename First, Commit Second
nodes.rationale: The reverse ordering leaves the database pointing at a path that does not exist, which every read then hits. A disk ahead of the database is a repair job; a database ahead of the disk is a broken grid — and metadata.json is what makes the surviving window recoverable.

nodes.label: migrate_storage Job
nodes.rationale: sqlx runs a migration in one transaction at startup; copying 23 GB is not that, and it needs a worker the migration cannot assume is running. It copies before it deletes, so an interrupted run has the file at both paths and never at neither.

nodes.label: part_move Audit Table
nodes.rationale: A move is not a revision: a revision is an immutable content-addressed snapshot, and a move changes no bytes, so it would produce a revision identical to its parent in every measured column and fill the version strip with zero-delta entries that are not design changes.

nodes.label: SourceRelocator
nodes.rationale: A third handle that can rename and nothing else. A directory rename parses nothing, reads no bytes and invokes no kernel, so routing an O(1) syscall through the job queue would honour the rule's letter against its reason and put a poll cycle between dragging a card and the card arriving. If it ever grows a method that reads or writes contents, that is the signal it has become SourceStore.

nodes.label: nulls not distinct Folder Uniqueness
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL treats NULLs as distinct in a unique constraint by default, so a plain unique constraint silently permits two root categories both named Terrain — the first thing a corpus scan produces. Verified against the project's own PostgreSQL 18.6 rather than asserted.

nodes.label: The 0009 Folder Tree Backfill
nodes.rationale: The tempting claim that every pre-0009 part sits at the library root was true before slice 6a and is false after it. Skipping it strands every existing library permanently flat with no user-reachable repair, because folders are created only for files that actually ingest and a re-scan settles everything as Skipped. A level-by-level loop, not one recursive CTE, because a CTE cannot use the ids it just generated as the next level's parents.

nodes.label: The Scan Creates Categories, After the Short-Circuit
nodes.rationale: Get-or-create is insert ... on conflict do nothing then select, because two workers scanning concurrently genuinely race the same directory. Creating categories during the walk would mean a re-scan of a directory whose models have all been moved away silently re-creates the now-empty originals, on disk as well as in the database.
nodes.norm_label: the scan creates categories, after the short-circuit

nodes.label: Soft Delete Cascades Through Subcategories
nodes.rationale: Deleting Terrain while it holds Terrain/Rocks/Cliffs must not leave Rocks alive and unreachable. Nothing is removed from disk, and the confirmation says three things: the count, that nothing is removed from the storage folder, and that it is reversible.

nodes.label: Source Dedup Is Gone, and ref_count Loses an Implication
nodes.rationale: ref_count still counts how many file rows reference a hash; what it no longer implies is one copy on disk. The consequence lands on purge: a purge that deleted 'the blob' would take another model's file.
nodes.norm_label: source dedup is gone, and ref_count loses an implication

nodes.label: Slice 6a — A Real Corpus Survives, and Files Go In From a Browser
nodes.rationale: Closes the pipeline's input end: a nested corpus could not be scanned at all, and ingest read whole files into memory.
nodes.norm_label: slice 6a — a real corpus survives, and files go in from a browser

nodes.label: Recursive Ingest Walk (depth 16)
nodes.rationale: Depth 16 is not a loop guard — symlinked directories are not followed, which is free because DirEntry::file_type() does not traverse — but a bound on pathological nesting and bind mounts that can cycle. Dot-entries are skipped; unreadable subdirectories are logged and skipped, because one unreadable folder must not cost the other 3,999 files. The whole relative path sorts, not the basename.

nodes.label: Identity Moves From the Name to the Path
nodes.rationale: Recursion alone is silent data loss: brackets/bracket.stl and plates/bracket.stl both become the part 'bracket', the second violates the name constraint, and classify_write maps that to Skipped — so the file is reported as already here and never indexed. Two parts called bracket in different folders is the truth, and the path is what tells them apart. All three sites move in one commit.
nodes.norm_label: identity moves from the name to the path

nodes.label: Migration 0007 — source_path
nodes.rationale: Backfilled from existing rows, which are all flat by construction because the scan that created them could not descend; a part with no source file row falls back to name alone, so the backfill cannot strand a row.

nodes.label: Streaming Instead of Buffering
nodes.rationale: The mesh kernel needs the whole mesh in memory to tessellate, so ingest goes from two copies to one rather than to none; download can go to constant memory because it only forwards bytes. Measured: streaming peaks at 5.7 MB against 385.8 MB buffering the same 380 MB blob. Reverting it is behaviourally identical and no test can catch it, which is why the criterion is a measurement.

nodes.label: The Verification Promise Changes Shape
nodes.rationale: Verifying before the first byte is buffering, so streaming cannot keep it. Bytes are hashed incrementally and a mismatch closes the body early, with Content-Length from blob.size_bytes so a short read is detectable. The promise moves from 'we never begin sending unverified bytes' to 'we never finish a download whose bytes did not verify'.

nodes.label: SourceWriter
nodes.rationale: The mirror of SourceReader, and the reasoning comes out the other way round: gating this behind WorkerRole would hand the api get and remove on every source blob in order to buy a put. Verification lives in the store, not the route, because 'store these bytes and they must hash to X' is the content-addressed store's own invariant and a route that verified separately would read a 2 GB file twice.

nodes.label: Probe / Chunk / Commit Upload Routes
nodes.rationale: The probe answers three lists rather than DATA.md's two, because the second win is the larger one: re-importing a folder into a new library transfers nothing. Commit is one batch for the whole folder — committing per file would give a folder of 500 parts 500 progress bars.

nodes.label: The Staging File's Length Is the Session State
nodes.rationale: No session table, no session id, no expiry sweep and no in-memory map. Resuming is offset = length; a wrong offset is a 409 carrying the length the server actually has, so a client that lost track is told rather than guessed at. The hash is the session id and is parsed as 64 lowercase hex before it reaches the filesystem, so there is no client string in that path at all.
nodes.norm_label: the staging file's length is the session state

nodes.label: The api Inserts the blob Row at ref_count 0
nodes.rationale: Splitting the write and the mesh across two processes creates a new orphan class the reap-on-failure trick cannot reach, because the failing process did not write the bytes and must not assume it may delete them. A blob row with count zero is collectable by slice 7's reaper; an orphan with no row at all is invisible to it forever. It also makes the worker's arm shorter, because link_existing then runs unchanged.
nodes.norm_label: the api inserts the blob row at ref_count 0

nodes.label: path_escapes Predicate in lapidary-core
nodes.rationale: One predicate, two doors: the scan payload joins against ingest_dir, and a client-supplied source_path goes into part.source_path and from there into a Content-Disposition filename. A guard on the caller rather than on the door is the shape that leaves a sibling caller unprotected.

nodes.label: webkitRelativePath Keeps the Dropped Folder's First Segment
nodes.rationale: Stripping it makes two dropped folders collide on a shared basename, which the source_path constraint turns into one part indexed and one silently skipped. readEntries also returns at most 100 entries per call, so calling it once reads the first hundred files of a parts library and drops the rest.
nodes.norm_label: webkitrelativepath keeps the dropped folder's first segment

nodes.label: Slice 6b — The Part You Clicked, and a Grid That Holds a Thousand
nodes.rationale: The premise was wrong once already: the grid is not slow, it is incomplete. Measured at 16 ms warm against an 80 ms budget, while fetchParts asked for one page and never asked for another, so a library of 1,000 parts showed 50. Paging is the requirement; virtualization is the optimization it enables.
nodes.norm_label: slice 6b — the part you clicked, and a grid that holds a thousand

nodes.label: useInfiniteQuery Cursor Paging
nodes.rationale: PartsPage.next is already a PartId or null, which is exactly getNextPageParam's contract, so nothing on the server changes. More pages are fetched by an IntersectionObserver sentinel rather than a button, because a grid is a scrolling surface and the gesture that means 'show me more' is scrolling to the end of it.

nodes.label: content-visibility: auto Instead of a Virtualizer
nodes.rationale: A virtualizer is a dependency, a measured scroll container, and a fight with a responsive auto-fill grid whose column count changes with the viewport. One CSS rule measured 8.8 ms against 128.4 ms for a cold full-page scroll pass over 1,000 cards — 14.6x, no dependency, and the grid stays a plain CSS grid. contain-intrinsic-size is 26rem, not the 20rem first guessed from a card measured before its thumbnail loaded.
nodes.norm_label: content-visibility: auto instead of a virtualizer

nodes.label: PartSummary.tessellation_l0
nodes.rationale: Without it the L0 glTF every ingest writes is unreachable and GET /api/blob/{blake3} has no possible caller. It is a hash, not a URL, and holding it is not authorization — derivative_is_reachable is what makes the field safe to hand out.

nodes.label: GET /api/parts/{id} — PartDetail
nodes.rationale: Every mesh-derived figure goes over the wire as {value, provenance} rather than a bare number with a badge computed beside it, because a bare number with a separate boolean is how the label gets lost when B-rep figures arrive on the same part in Phase 2. An open mesh reports no volume at all, in words.

nodes.label: SSE Batch Events Stream
nodes.rationale: react-query does not poll a hidden document, so the progress line froze on a hidden tab. It is LISTEN/NOTIFY with a timer floor, for the reason slice 2 wrote down. The stream ends itself when the batch does, because EventSource reconnects automatically and a stream that merely goes quiet is one the browser will re-open forever. The poll stays as the fallback.

nodes.label: Migration-Seeded Example Part
nodes.rationale: A migration cannot mesh, so the seeded part carries its measurements and thumbnail as committed literals. It is a normal part, not a special one: no is_example column, no filter that hides it, no first-run flag — the row is the same shape ingest writes, so nothing downstream needs to know it arrived differently.

nodes.label: The Live-Fill Refetch Is Gated on Grid Depth
nodes.rationale: invalidateQueries on an infinite query refetches every page it holds, so the settle-effect pulled eleven pages per tick — roughly 4.7 MB a second — and bought nothing, because parts arrive newest-first ahead of every cursor already held. Trimming the cache to one page would be the other way, and it snaps a reading user back to the top.
nodes.norm_label: the live-fill refetch is gated on grid depth

nodes.label: The part_image Gallery Leaves Phase 1
nodes.rationale: Slice 4's argument — user data cannot live in SourceStore or DerivativeStore — is dissolved by the folder-tree layout, where a model becomes a real directory holding an images/ folder. The gallery belongs to whichever slice lands that layout, where it is one directory listing rather than a migration, an upload route and a UI rewritten weeks later.

nodes.label: Slice 7 — Delete That Is Not Deletion
nodes.rationale: A Phase-4 roadmap item pulled forward on the owner's priority call, shipping the subset a Phase-1 user can hit today: a library you can remove things from. Storage tiering stays in Phase 4, because tiering is what makes quarantine's physical layout matter.
nodes.norm_label: slice 7 — delete that is not deletion

nodes.label: DELETE /api/parts/{id} — Soft Delete
nodes.rationale: One UPDATE, because every read path already filters part.deleted_at IS NULL, so hiding the part needs no query changes.

nodes.label: POST /api/parts/{id}/restore
nodes.rationale: Undelete stays explicit, for the reason delete does: we do not un-delete implicitly either.

nodes.label: A Re-Scan Does Not Resurrect a Deleted Part
nodes.rationale: library_holds must keep not filtering deleted_at — the load-bearing exception. Deleting from the index is a decision; a scan re-adding it would make delete useless. Both branches already produce it: unchanged bytes hit the hash short-circuit, changed bytes hit the source_path constraint and classify_write. Zero code, and untested until this slice.
nodes.norm_label: a re-scan does not resurrect a deleted part

nodes.label: Purge Recomputes ref_count, Never Decrements
nodes.rationale: A counter maintained only by arithmetic drifts, and the thing that acts on the drift deletes bytes. Recomputing from reachability makes drift self-heal on the one path that matters. The doomed hashes are collected before the delete, because afterwards there is no path from the part to its blobs; and it is not a race, because UPDATE blob SET ref_count = (subquery) takes the same row lock ingest's +1 takes.

nodes.label: Quarantine Is a Timestamp, Not a quarantine/ Tree
nodes.rationale: Deviates from DATA.md 1.6. Restore is then free — clearing the column restores the blob — where a physical move needs the reverse move and needs every reader to know a second location, a second lookup on the hot path to serve a case that is supposed to be rare. And the store's layout is about to move anyway.
nodes.norm_label: quarantine is a timestamp, not a quarantine/ tree

nodes.label: The 30-Day Reaper Sweep
nodes.rationale: Re-asks reachability inside the transaction that deletes the row and the file. On day one it removes nothing, because no row is 30 days old; the destructive path is proved with an injected cutoff, never a wall clock. Re-ingest un-quarantines by existing.

nodes.label: The Schema Is the Safety Property, Not the WHERE Clause
nodes.rationale: Corrected by the mutation proof: dropping the NOT EXISTS pair for ref_count = 0 does not lose bytes, because file.blake3 and derivative.blake3 are foreign keys to blob and the DELETE raises a constraint violation instead. What the pair buys is availability — the sweep is one transaction, so one wrongly-quarantined blob would otherwise roll back every legitimate removal beside it, every hour, forever, with a log line as the only symptom.
nodes.norm_label: the schema is the safety property, not the where clause

nodes.label: The Eviction Wording Boundary
nodes.rationale: Three actions, three vocabularies. Eviction is not a deletion with softer words: it removes only bytes we produced and can reproduce, which is why it is the one of the three that needs no undo. The strings are cheaper to get right before there are two of them.

nodes.label: LibraryStorage.removed_bytes
nodes.rationale: Both storage totals exclude soft-deleted parts, so a removal dropped the number while the disk held the same bytes — a panel reporting a removal as a saving, the one claim this area must never make. Quarantined bytes are not in it and cannot be: a purged blob has no part and therefore no library, library-less by construction rather than unimplemented.

nodes.label: ref_count Is Non-Load-Bearing for Destructive Decisions
nodes.rationale: The response to a corpus audit that covered only the simple path was not a bigger corpus but removing the counter from every destructive decision, so the audit's coverage stops gating the slice. A drifted counter can waste disk or trigger a quarantine the reaper declines to complete; it cannot destroy a reachable blob. The counter becomes a fast hint and a number to show the user.
nodes.norm_label: ref_count is non-load-bearing for destructive decisions

nodes.label: A Part With Zero Revisions Is in Neither List
nodes.rationale: page's revision LATERAL is an inner join, so such a part would be beyond reach once removed. Closing it means a LEFT JOIN and a null case on every downstream field of the grid's hottest query, for a state nothing in Phase 1 produces. Phase 2, which is the first thing that can create one, owns it.
nodes.norm_label: a part with zero revisions is in neither list

nodes.label: A Purge That Removes the Model Directory
nodes.rationale: PgBlobs::reap unlinks the content-addressed path, which since the folder tree is only the address of files migrate_storage has not reached. Nothing is lost, which is the right way round for this area to fail; what breaks is the promise that bytes are kept 30 days and then deleted.
nodes.norm_label: a purge that removes the model directory

nodes.label: quarantined_file table
nodes.rationale: Keyed on the store-relative path, not on blob: blob is one row per hash and source dedup is gone, so one hash can be several model files with several independent lifetimes and a per-hash column could describe at most one of them. No foreign key to blob, because a blake3 column that refused to outlive its blob row would lose the only record of the path. The index is plain, not partial, because every row is quarantined by construction.

nodes.label: The Clock Belongs to the Bytes
nodes.rationale: A hash identifies its bytes, so a second purge touching an already-quarantined blob must not restart the hold; a path does not identify its bytes, so on conflict the clock restarts. Reaching the conflict takes a person, and what puts it back in play is the store being browsable — delete the model directory in a file manager, re-scan, purge again, and the same path arrives holding different bytes.
nodes.norm_label: the clock belongs to the bytes

nodes.label: Unlink Before Commit, and Only the File Is Fatal
