nodes.rationale: A sweep that committed first would leave bytes with no row at all, which nothing would ever collect. File first means every partial state is 'the bytes are gone, the tidying is not finished', which the next sweep completes; removing metadata.json first would leave a directory holding bytes and no manifest, which reads as an orphan to anything walking the store.
nodes.norm_label: unlink before commit, and only the file is fatal

nodes.label: remove_dir_if_empty — Non-Fatal
nodes.rationale: Removing what the owner left in a directory they were promised they could edit is the data loss reaping exists to prevent; failing the sweep over it stops every other removal for as long as that file sits there. It is left reporting rather than insisting, because moving the decision into the function would take it away from both callers.

nodes.label: Phantom Blob Bytes in Both Reports
nodes.rationale: For a migrated source the blob row's stored_bytes describes a path migrate_storage emptied, so purge and reap count it twice over: 22,660 reported freed against 12,976 that actually left the volume. Left alone because correcting it means deciding what a blob row's size means for a hash with no content-addressed copy — the same question storage_totals defers — and the figure reaches an operator log and no user-facing string.
nodes.norm_label: phantom blob bytes in both reports

nodes.label: occt-bridge Sidecar
nodes.rationale: A separate process rather than a linked library, so an OCCT crash takes down one job instead of the worker. Empty until Phase 0b.

nodes.label: OcctKernel
nodes.rationale: Arrives in Phase 0b behind the same Kernel trait, with OCCT built from source in the worker image; the trait does not change.

nodes.label: Mesh Input Yields No Analytic Entities
nodes.rationale: The invariant that stops tessellated numbers from being presented as exact. KernelOutput's fields are explicitly not stable — the Phase 0a shape is a placeholder for one carrying blob references and analytic entities with axes, radii and normals instead of opaque strings.
nodes.norm_label: mesh input yields no analytic entities

nodes.label: Lapidary SPA Shell
nodes.rationale: A static HTML shell mounting #root and loading /src/main.tsx as a module — the Vite SPA entry point, with no server-rendered markup.

nodes.label: Dark-Only Root Class
nodes.rationale: class="dark" is hardcoded on <html>: dark only, no light mode and no theme toggle, so there is nothing to switch.

nodes.label: Slice 7 Handoff
nodes.rationale: Lapidary can now remove things; before this slice it could index 1,703 files and delete none of them.

nodes.label: What the Slice 7 Audit Did Not Prove
nodes.rationale: Recomputing every ref_count across the 150-part corpus agreed 300/300, and that proves less than it looks like: the corpus has zero shared blobs so it never took the link_existing branch — exactly where a reference counter drifts — no rung was ever re-rendered, and there is one library.
nodes.norm_label: what the slice 7 audit did not prove

nodes.label: Slice 7 Mutation Ledger (M7-1 … M7-5)
nodes.rationale: Five mutations, each reverted byte-identically, each named with the test that caught it — including the reaper's NOT EXISTS pair, whose removal made a drifted-high blob immortal and let one bad row take the whole sweep down.

nodes.label: Re-Ingest Un-Quarantines Immediately, Not Within the Hour
nodes.rationale: Never unsafe, because the reaper re-checks reachability — but 'a referenced blob is never quarantined' was true only eventually. quarantined_at = NULL now rides on the ref_count + 1 statement every ingest already runs against that row.
nodes.norm_label: re-ingest un-quarantines immediately, not within the hour

nodes.label: HEAD Warming last_accessed_at Needed No Code
nodes.rationale: axum::routing::get answers HEAD with the same handler and strips the body, so the touch was always there. A test pins it, because that is a property of a routing helper that swapping get for an explicit MethodFilter would silently remove.
nodes.norm_label: head warming last_accessed_at needed no code

nodes.label: After the Folder Tree — What Phase 1 Still Owes
nodes.rationale: A planning document, not a spec: it says what is left and why one thing goes before another, and stops short of designing any of it.
nodes.norm_label: after the folder tree — what phase 1 still owes

nodes.label: Phase 1 Is Feature-Complete and Unmeasured
nodes.rationale: Every clause of the exit criterion has code behind it and none has a number: the corpus on this machine is 156 parts, not 1,000, and nothing has ever timed a warm grid page. The suite proves the mechanisms; it does not prove the criterion, because the criterion is about a size and a latency and the tests use neither. Measure after search, not before — measuring a query you are about to rewrite buys a number with a short shelf life.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Search Gap
nodes.rationale: lapidary-index is a twenty-line stub and the tsvector column and pg_trgm extension are read by nothing. The largest remaining item and the one a person notices first: a grid that pages through 1,000 parts but cannot find one is a filing cabinet with no labels — and the folder tree makes that sharper, because now there are categories to search within. Build the Phase 2 identifier-aware ranking seam now even if only the simple half is wired.

nodes.label: More Than One Library
nodes.rationale: The web hard-codes DEFAULT_LIBRARY_ID and there is no create route; LibraryMode is exported and read by nothing. Smaller than it sounds on the server and mostly a front-end job — a switcher, and a decision about what the URL looks like when a library is selectable.

nodes.label: Per-Library Page Size and Card Density
nodes.rationale: Two more fields on a settings row that already exists plus the controls; the one item a user asks for by name once a library gets big.
nodes.norm_label: per-library page size and card density

nodes.label: A Category Rename Never Moves Bytes
nodes.rationale: Answered no on 2026-09-07. A user renaming WIP to Archive 2024 may not expect ten thousand files rewritten, and that is the case that decided it. It is not a rename that declines to tidy up — it is a rule about what a directory name is: folder.slug is the address allocated at creation, folder.name is the label. Letting the slug track the name would be strictly worse than a stale directory name, because nothing rewrites file.storage_path and a category would end up split across one directory per rename it had ever had. Enforced rather than documented: PgFolders::rename has no slug parameter.
nodes.norm_label: a category rename never moves bytes

nodes.label: file.storage_path Stays Nullable
nodes.rationale: Decided against on 2026-09-07. The estimate was wrong twice over: seven sites, not four, and migrate_storage exists only to fill those nulls, so NOT NULL makes it unable to ever find work while enqueue_migration_if_absent gates on 'no pending job', so every worker boot would queue a permanent no-op. That narrows the upgrade path to two hops for any store predating 0009, and a two-hop upgrade for air-gapped deployments is a real operational cost; seven tested branches reading as defensive is not.

nodes.label: Catalogue Test — Every Table Referencing the Part Chain
nodes.rationale: Purging a part that had ever been moved answered 500, because part_move references part and arrived a slice after purge's delete list was written; neither suite could see it. The delete list is maintained by hand precisely because nothing declares ON DELETE CASCADE, so the test asks the catalogue what has a foreign key into part, revision, file or derivative and fails when purge does not delete from it — naming the table and saying what to add.
nodes.norm_label: catalogue test — every table referencing the part chain

nodes.label: slugify Is a Filesystem-Safety Function, Not a URL Slug
nodes.rationale: A category's directory keeps its spaces and capitals because the store is meant to be legible to a person opening it in a file manager. The route derives the slug and never accepts one from a client, and the move route reads the stored slug back rather than re-slugging a name, so the two cannot drift.
nodes.norm_label: slugify is a filesystem-safety function, not a url slug

nodes.label: The Sweep Over-Reports What It Freed
nodes.rationale: By exactly the stored_bytes of a migrated source's blob row — a figure describing a content-addressed path migrate_storage emptied. Measured: 22,660 reported against 12,976 actually freed. Pre-existing, reaching an operator log and no user-facing string.
nodes.norm_label: the sweep over-reports what it freed

nodes.label: Folder Tree and Moves — Follow-Ups
nodes.rationale: The leftovers, ordered by what would hurt most to forget. None of it blocks a merge: every item is a known, written-down edge rather than a bug in what shipped.

nodes.label: repath_category Job (proposed, later refused)
nodes.rationale: Shaped like migrate_storage — resumable, one model directory at a time, an UPDATE per move so a crash costs one directory rather than the walk. The route enqueues; the worker walks. Re-pathing hundreds of directories is also not work an HTTP handler should hold open, and deploy.rs's RELOCATE_MODULE structurally forbids a folder handler from re-pathing a subtree.

nodes.label: The Descendant CTE Lives in the Page Query
nodes.rationale: The brief said implement it in PgFolders; it went inline into PgParts::page instead — one query rather than two round trips, and one descent implementation rather than two to keep in step. Settled as accepted after the merge, because splitting it now would create the second descent implementation the original note was worried about.
nodes.norm_label: the descendant cte lives in the page query

nodes.label: Two Tree Scale Ceilings
nodes.rationale: PgFolders::tree pairs every folder with each descendant in one recursive CTE — O(nodes x depth) rows, depth bounded at 16 — and the tree is fetched whole on every sidebar load by design, because a lazy tree costs a round trip per expand on the interaction that has to feel instant. Hundreds of categories is nothing; tens of thousands would want a materialised count or a closure table. Measure before rewriting.

nodes.label: GET /api/parts/{id}/moves Has No Consumer
nodes.rationale: It also answers [] for a part id that names nothing, which is the same answer as 'this part has never moved' — deliberate, because nothing acts differently on the two and telling them apart costs a query on every read of a legitimately empty history. If a history is ever shown, the 404 starts to matter and should be added at the same time.

nodes.label: No UI for Creating or Renaming a Category
nodes.rationale: The routes are built and server-tested with no web consumer. Create depends on nothing and is the smallest real feature; rename needs prose create does not, because the directory keeps its original name and a person who renames Terain to Terrain will otherwise go looking for the fixed spelling. A PATCH carrying both a new name and a new parent applies the move first and the rename second and answers 409 renamedAfterMove — a branch with no test because no client sends both fields.
nodes.norm_label: no ui for creating or renaming a category
